# Verdicts and rankings (living file)

Purpose: the end goal of all research. Who beats whom, who's better, who's the best.
Each verdict has: the matchup or ranking, the verdict, confidence (low/med/high), the key reasoning chain (feats, fights, statements with primary sources), the weak spots or what could flip it, and the date last updated.
Update whenever new notes change the picture. Form verdicts independently from evidence; forum opinions are reference only.

## Star Wars (Legends) head-to-heads


### Strongest Star Wars Legends character (best guess, Oct 11, 2026; version note and novel cite added 2026-10-19). Confidence: low-medium
- Verdict: if the Mortis gods count, the Father/Son are on top, since they're literal Force embodiments. Among actual Force users, Vitiate/Valkorion is #1, with Sidious (Dark Empire peak) a close #2 and Abeloth in that range.
- Vitiate: the Nathema ritual ate every living thing on a whole planet, and Ziost got devoured. He also lived for over 1,000 years by jumping bodies, and he was "infinitely more powerful than Darth Nyriss" (vitiate-comicvine-respect-part1.txt; verified in the novel: «the Emperor was infinitely more powerful than Darth Nyriss had ever been», Revan, Ch28, L6001). The Nathema Force void is corroborated on page (Revan, Ch15, L3239-3283; Ch18, L3731, L3803).
- Sidious: has the most "most powerful Sith ever" accolades (Death Star novel, Darth Maul: Sith Apprentice, Insider #86), plus growth after ROTJ (the Dark Empire Force storms; "grown very strong... so have I"). Downside: the accolades are statements, and Vitiate's planet-scale feats beat his showings on feats.
- What could flip it: the Sith-rank argument (accolades cap Vitiate as a Sith), and whether the Ones count as characters or as Force entities.
- Versions (added 2026-10-19): peak versions by default, amps included for this ranking. Vitiate's #1 slot is the post-Nathema Emperor at his SWTOR/Valkorion peak. Ladder: base Emperor (3,951 BBY) < the Emperor feeding on Revan (Revan, Ch29, L6189 on: «Revan could feel the Emperor feeding on him, drawing on his power to sate his endless hunger») < SWTOR/Valkorion. The Revan novel by itself shows only the base and fed versions and does not put him above Dark Empire Sidious; that comes from the SWTOR/Ziost material. Sidious at #2 is Dark Empire Sidious, an amped version.

### Caedus (Jacen, 40 ABY) vs Lumiya (Oct 11, 2026). Confidence: high
- Verdict: Jacen wins. Lumiya is ahead in Sith technique and long-range manipulation, but she is physically capped. Jacen has more raw power and the higher ceiling.
- Reasoning: Bloodlines frames Jacen as the stronger one in their sparring and training (lotf-2 L6243, L6305, L8543). Lumiya says her cybernetic body limits her, and she contrasts herself with Sidious, who «had no limit» (Tempest L2716-2720). She also says she knows the Sith Master's coordination power but «can just never wield it» (Exile L6759). Lobi was pushing her back one on one (Tempest L1668).
- What could flip it: a prepared Lumiya using her phantom and possession techniques (Exile Ch10) or the Sith sphere in Sacrifice. She also senses things better than Jacen.

### Caedus (Jacen) vs Mara Jade Skywalker (Oct 11, 2026; updated with LotF 5-8 on Oct 17, 2026). Confidence: medium
- Verdict: Jacen/Caedus wins most fair fights on Force power. Mara with prep and her own terrain is a real threat who can nearly kill him. Canon outcome: Jacen kills her in Sacrifice Ch21. Against post-Sacrifice Darth Caedus, who is stronger after her death, Mara's odds drop further.
- Reasoning: Mara says Jacen's powers are «way beyond mine» (Bloodlines L837), that «It'll take both of us» to stop him (Tempest L4220), and that he is «too powerful already» (Tempest L5696). In Sacrifice she admits she «couldn't outstrip his Force powers» (L7444). Even so, she ambushed him, buried him, and was beating him when he won with an illusion of Ben's face and a poison dart (lotf-5 Duel C, L8358-8545). Jacen concedes she «shouldn't have been able to get near him» (Sacrifice L8487). In Inferno, Caedus's own POV admits «Mara had demonstrated when she nearly killed him on Kavan» (Inferno L2011, lotf-6 S7). His Sith battle-sight only arrives after her death (Sacrifice L9293-9299). Fury adds no new fight; Ben's suspicion (Fury L1803) keeps the Kavan result central.
- What could flip it: count only the Kavan fight's flow before the dart and Mara looks like the winner. In an open-field fight, the power gap decides it. Caedus's growth (Inferno, Fury) pushes it further toward him.
- Revelation (LotF 8) adds this: Caedus's own recorded confession to Shevu says «she brought down the ceiling and she was like a madwoman ... I had lightsaber, blaster, and crush in-juries, and the only way I could stop her was to use the poison darts I keep as a last line of defense» (Revelation L7501). Privately he thinks «If I hadn't killed her, I'd be the one getting a state funeral now» (L3281). Fett, after watching the recording: «nearly got his backside handed to him by Skywalker's wife. He still looks scared when he remembers it» (L7669). This confirms that the Kavan fight was going Mara's way until the poison. The verdict doesn't change: power still favors Caedus, and Kavan shows what Mara can do with prep (lotf-8-revelation-notes.md S10-S13).

### Luke vs Jacen (status at 40 ABY, LotF 2-4) (Oct 11, 2026). Confidence: medium-high
- Verdict: Luke is ahead through Exile, but Jacen is closing fast. Jacen is already better at deceiving and hiding.
- Reasoning: Luke senses Jacen closing in but still above him (Bloodlines L6653). Mara still calls Luke «the most accomplished lightsaber artist in the galaxy» (Exile L165). Jacen deceives Luke repeatedly (Exile L2355, L2377), and Omas hypes him (Exile L589; a politician). Jacen fears a vengeful Luke (Sacrifice L6948).
- What could flip it: Caedus's growth after Sacrifice (Inferno onward). This entry covers the LotF 2-4 status only.

### Caedus vs Luke (post-Sacrifice, LotF 5-7: Darth Caedus) (Oct 11, 2026; updated with LotF 8-9 on Oct 17, 2026). Confidence: high (was medium-high)
- Verdict: Luke wins. He beat Caedus on-page in Inferno and is consistently ranked above him. Allston's Fury narrows the gap, so this is not high confidence.
- Reasoning: Inferno Ch11: Luke Force-pins Caedus «with no visible effort» (lotf-6 Fight A, L2559-2639). Inferno Ch19: Luke beats Caedus in the Embrace-of-Pain duel. Caedus's own POV says «Luke had beaten him» and admits Luke had escaped the garrote before Ben's stab (Inferno L4961), and that «his uncle had nearly killed him» (L5067). Luke out-hides him: «Not even Jacen had that kind of control.» (Inferno L4741). Sacrifice: Lumiya, «Luke can still take you in a lightsaber fight.» (L3958). Fury: Caedus calls himself «the best lightsaber swordsman around-excepting possibly Luke» (L1717). Corran ranks Luke #1 and Jacen #2 (L783). The Inferno injuries took weeks to heal (Fury L5573). Luke out-senses him and hits the stealth Blur by feel (Fury L3215).
- What could flip it: Inferno's win came with surprise (Luke was believed dead), Luke's rage, and Ben's dagger finishing it. Allston's Fury retells the duel as even from Caedus's POV (L345), and Luke's own POV calls a fresh Caedus «Luke's match» (Fury L6729). Caedus's TK removed Saba from the bridge fight (L6629). Caedus is still growing (Revelation, Invincible are unread here). If a later book shows a healed Caedus winning cleanly, drop this to medium.
- LotF 8-9 update (Oct 17, 2026): no later book shows a healed Caedus beating Luke, so the downgrade condition was not met. Revelation and Invincible point the other way:
  - Revelation Ch12, the StealthX duel at Fondor. Luke hides from Caedus's senses entirely («Luke-he could always sense Luke», L5281). He rips Caedus's fighter apart through the Force: «Caedus tried to block Luke in the Force and suddenly got an idea of just how much power Luke could muster» (L5335), and Caedus's chest cracks. Luke says «If I wanted to kill you, I could have done it several times over by now» (L5299). Caedus escapes only by threatening a civilian tunnel. The caveats are that it was a fighter duel, not a saber duel, and Luke had a wingmate.
  - Invincible. Luke's foresight on fighting Caedus himself: «"It's worse," Luke said. "I win."» (L1505). Caedus's own POV calls Luke «the one swordsman in the galaxy whom Caedus did not dare fight one-armed» (L2515). Of Inferno he thinks he «barely managed to survive» (L2519). Seeing Luke's fighter, «his intestines had filled with ice» (L4382). Luke Force-shears a blast door's thirty-centimeter locking pins (L5680).
  - Net: Fury's «Luke's match» is the outlier; it comes from Allston's POV framing and isn't backed by Revelation or Invincible. Luke > Caedus, high confidence. The remaining weak spot is that there is no straight one-on-one saber duel between a fully healthy Caedus and Luke after Inferno (lotf-8-revelation-notes.md Fight A; lotf-9-invincible-notes.md S1, S3-S5).

### Jaina Solo vs Caedus (as of Fury, end of 40 ABY) (Oct 11, 2026). Confidence: medium
- Verdict: at the end of Fury, Caedus beats Jaina. She is the top Knight but not yet Master-tier. Her later win in Invincible comes from Mandalorian anti-Jedi training that Fury explicitly sets up, not from parity in raw power.
- Reasoning: Zekk: «I doubt any Jedi Knight can stand against you. You need to practice against a Master.» (Fury L1957). Jaina herself: «I have as much power as he does. ... potentially. But he's had training I haven't.» (Fury L7039). Jag, who just killed Alema: «Jacen. ... he's far more dangerous.» (L7041). In the Inferno dogfight, «Her brother seemed to anticipate every shot before she took it.» (Inferno L4303). Caedus beat a Master plus three Knights at once while still hurt (Fury L1545-1745). Jag's lesson, «you need to be thinking like someone who hunts Jedi. Like me.» (Fury L2115), and his prep-based kill of Alema show the route she takes. Fury ends with her going «Toward her teacher.» (L7067). See jaina-solo-quotes.txt L17, L30, L34 for the later duel.
- What could flip it: Invincible, where Jaina actually kills Caedus (now read; see the Invincible-era entry below, Oct 17, 2026). For the Invincible-era matchup the verdict should flip toward Jaina on the strength of her prep and Caedus's state of mind. This entry covers the Fury-era status only.

### Jaina Solo vs Darth Caedus (Invincible era, 41 ABY) (Oct 17, 2026). Confidence: high for the in-book result; medium for a neutral rematch
- Verdict: Jaina beats the Caedus of Invincible. On-page she kills him alone in the Anakin Solo's biodisposal pit (Invincible Ch18, L5088-5186). In a neutral fight between a healthy, focused Caedus and the fully prepared Jaina, I still favor Caedus slightly on raw power. Her preparation and his habit of underrating her make it close, so that part is medium confidence.
- Reasoning, for Jaina:
  - Preparation: Fett and Beviin's anti-Jedi training (Revelation Ch7-9) and shatterpoint. She crumbles raw beskar with her fingertips (Invincible L3896-3906), matching Caedus's own feat (L2305-2309).
  - Concealment: Caedus can't feel her (Revelation L3383; Invincible L4498, L5112).
  - Earlier wins: she broke an exhausted Caedus's Force choke on Mirta (Revelation L7027). At Nickel One she took his arm, though boosted by Luke (see below).
  - The final duel: she guts him at the door (L5100-5102), outlasts lightning, the incinerator pull and his melee edge, then cuts his Achilles tendon (L5172) and kills him (L5186). She does it explicitly without Luke's boost: «she would have to fight in a different way-her own way» (L5004).
  - Author framing: the Sword of the Jedi destiny (Invincible L799, L5632-5640) and the love-not-anger power surge (L5154).
- Reasoning, for Caedus (why this isn't "Jaina > Caedus" outright):
  - Statements: Jaina herself says «He's magnitudes stronger than me in the Force» (L4836), and «the fact that her brother remained standing at all proved how much greater his Force powers were than her own» (L2592).
  - Conditions of the final duel: Caedus is one-armed (stump, L3590; «lacking a second hand», L5086), gut-stabbed in the first second, and distracted by the nanokiller threat to Allana («I'm trying to save Tenel Ka and Allana», L5140). At the end he stops defending to warn Tenel Ka through the Force (L5182-5184). Even so, he led the melee («anticipating her every move», L5112), broke her forearm and cheekbone, cut her abdomen, and nearly incinerated her (L5150).
  - Nickel One was not Jaina alone: Luke's body was empty (L2469). Caedus felt «Luke one moment, Jaina the next, and then they had both been there» (L3688), and Jaina's power drained afterwards (L2598).
- What could flip it: a healthy Caedus who takes her seriously (he dismissed her: «My sister is nothing to be concerned with», L4404). Counting raw power above everything else would also favor him. Counting Nickel One as a Jaina-solo feat would push the neutral rematch to Jaina.
- Supersedes the Fury-era entry above only for 41 ABY. That entry still stands for end-of-40-ABY Jaina (lotf-9-invincible-notes.md Section 6; lotf-8-revelation-notes.md Section 6).

### Darth Caedus, final tier (complete LotF primary read, LotF 1 added 2026-10-18) (Oct 17, 2026). Confidence: medium
- Verdict: high Master / Sith Lord, placed at the top of tier 5 just below LotF Luke. Not tier 4.
- His breadth is unmatched among his peers:
  - He drops Fondor's planetary shield by mass mind-influence, fed by fleet battle meditation (Revelation L6001-6023).
  - Shatterpoint (Invincible L2305), Aing-Tii fighting-sight (L2503), Nightsister blood-trail tracking (L3688), Force lightning, flow-walking.
  - He stays lethal while crippled: kills Mandalorian commandos one-armed (L2327-2347) and stands up after losing the arm (L2586).
- His ceiling is capped:
  - Luke beats him (Inferno; Revelation Fight A; Invincible S1, S3-S5).
  - The big feats drain him, and he admits «No, I am not omnipotent» (Revelation L7083).
  - Collective Jedi concealment and non-Force preparation beat him (Revelation L5849; the kneecapping at L7143).
  - A prepared Knight killed him while he was crippled.
- Why not tier 4: nothing he does approaches Yoda, Plagueis or Krayt-level showings, and Luke (tier 5) is above him. His earlier tier-4 slot was a placeholder written before LotF 8-9 were read.
- LotF 1 (Betrayal) is now read (2026-10-18, lotf-1-betrayal-notes.md). It confirms the ceiling: Luke's attack nearly kills Jacen (Betrayal L7499, L7511-7513), and Jacen is an elite Knight who kills Nelani (L8125). **The tier does not change.** Remaining weak spot: the DEEP (respect-thread) layer is missing.

### Starkiller (Galen Marek, TFU) vs Darth Vader (Oct 18, 2026). Confidence: medium
- Verdict: Galen wins at his peak.
- Death Star duel (TFU Ch38, L5409-5429): Vader goes for the kill and Galen beats him outright. Vader's earlier wins came from a stab in the back and the Corellia ambush.
- TFU2 clone (Ch25, L5327-5379): Vader breaks both sabers, but Starkiller wins with lightning and a TK disarm and Vader is captured. The Ch1 escape (L517, L545-547) points the same way.
- What could flip it: the Juno factor. Vader's hostage play makes Starkiller kneel (TFU2 L5209), and the decisive gash came from Juno (L5247). This is Vader from 2-1 BBY; his ROTJ/comics peak isn't tested here. Notes: tfu-1-notes.md, tfu-2-notes.md.

### Starkiller (Galen) vs Darth Sidious (Oct 18, 2026). Confidence: high
- Verdict: Sidious wins.
- Palpatine kneels on purpose to tempt Galen (TFU L5459) and survives the final detonation. Galen's achievement is tanking his lightning long enough to let the Rebels escape, and he dies doing it. The Wookieepedia Sidious extraction says the same (legends-feats.md).

### Starkiller vs Luke (LotF) / Darth Caedus (Oct 18, 2026). Confidence: low
- Verdict: no firm call. Lean: Luke > Starkiller; Starkiller vs Caedus is roughly even, leaning Starkiller on raw TK and lightning output, with Caedus favored on breadth (battle meditation, shatterpoint, flow-walking).
- Reasoning: there is no shared opponent apart from Vader-vs-Luke comparisons. LotF Luke beats Caedus repeatedly, and Galen's best showing is beating a 2 BBY Vader. Low confidence; this rests on cross-era scaling only.

### Luke vs Lumiya (Oct 11, 2026). Confidence: high
- Verdict: Luke wins.
- Reasoning: At Roqoo, Luke beat her even in a 2v1 with hostages at stake and after losing his hand: five blaster shots (Tempest L5892). She predicted she would lose (Tempest L4638) and says Luke will «hurt me ... until I die» (Exile L865). At Gilatter, the exchange was even and she disengaged (Exile L6555-6595). In Sacrifice he beats her on Terephon and beheads her (lotf-5 L9008-9034).
- Weak spot: two secondhand lines say she «fought Luke to a standstill» (Exile L3545, L4815). At Terephon she came to die (Sacrifice L8704).

### Mara vs Alema Rar (Oct 11, 2026). Confidence: high
- Verdict: Mara wins.
- Reasoning: Mara beat her at Roqoo: «not much of a challenge» (Tempest L5832). Alema's only edge was a distraction that cost Luke his hand. In Exile, Alema loses every direct contest: Leia reverses her dart (L5593), Leia drives her back (L6601), and Jag breaks her clavicle (L5641). What keeps her alive is erasing people's memories and running.
- What could flip it: Alema's stealth, ambush, and poison-dart opening. Her dart missed Mara in Exile (L3887).

### Strongest Legends character: revision note (2026-10-11, after SI t4404). Confidence unchanged (medium-low)
- The Vitiate #1 pick stands, a little firmer. Per the recency/"shedding limitations" point, the pre-2008 "most powerful Sith ever" lines for Sidious can't have counted Vitiate (created 2008-11), so the "accolades cap Vitiate" flip condition is weaker. ### Sidious (prime, ROTS to Dark Empire) vs Plagueis (prime, post-Maladian) (2026-10-11; revised 2026-10-19 after the Darth Plagueis read). Winner: Sidious (ROTS-era peak). Diff: high. Confidence: low-medium
- Versions (peak by default): Sidious = his peak after the boost he got from Plagueis's death (it starts in Darth Plagueis, Prologue, L117) through ROTS. Dark Empire Sidious is a separate, amped version and is NOT used for the main call; it only widens the gap. Plagueis = his prime, Part Three of Darth Plagueis (33–32 BBY), after the ~41 BBY "galactonic" shift (Ch24, L5445: «The evidence was in his own increased midi-chlorian count»). That amp is permanent, so it is included. TPM-era Sidious (33–32 BBY) is the pre-boost version.
- Verdict: Sidious wins at his ROTS-era peak. Against TPM-era (pre-boost) Sidious it's close to even, a slight Plagueis lean (high diff, low confidence).
- For Plagueis: author intent. James Luceno (Facebook Q&A): «If it had come to a duel, I think Plagueis may have found a way to undermine his apprentice.» (Del Rey Star Wars Books Facebook Q&A, Jan 25 2012; transcript: https://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/James_Luceno_Facebook_QA_Recap_143276.asp) In the novel Sidious is unsure: «Was he a level behind? Two levels behind?» (Darth Plagueis, Ch23, L5255; TPM-era Sidious judging prime Plagueis, so it counts for those two versions). The film framing (ROTS): «so powerful and so wise». Feats: an injured Force wave «all but atomized the bodies of six Maladians» (Darth Plagueis, Ch20, L4765; ~54 BBY Plagueis, before the shift amp, so a floor for his prime).
- For Sidious: Plagueis's death boosts him («the Force so strong within him», Darth Plagueis, Prologue, L117). He gets decades of growth after that («his own powers had increased tenfold over the decades», Darth Plagueis, Ch23, L5255; a TPM-era self-assessment). He has on-page wins over Windu, Kolar, Tiin and Fisto, and a standstill with Yoda (sidious-legends-quotes.txt). The Dark Empire Force storms belong to the amped DE version and are noted only. He killed Plagueis, though asleep and drunk, so that's no fight evidence.
- How the one "fight" went (Darth Plagueis, Ch30, L7207–7285): Plagueis was drunk and asleep. Sidious's lightning «ground itself on the Muun's breathing device», and Plagueis «stopped short of defending himself» (L7219). While suffocating he still raised a Force storm (L7243). He died by choke and suffocation. It was an ambush, not a duel, and it counts only for the drunk, dying Plagueis of that night.
- Luceno's framing: «An apprentice no longer needs to be stronger, you told me, merely more clever.» (Ch30, L7247). The book frames the murder as cleverness, not strength, so it doesn't settle the power question.
- Common link: both are rated against the same Jedi Council tier; Sidious has the actual on-page results.
- What could flip it: weight Luceno's quote as binding author intent, or use TPM-era Sidious.
- Forum (SI, opinion only): split 6 to 4 for Plagueis.

### Krayt (reborn, Legacy: War) vs Plagueis (2026-10-11). Confidence: low, slight Plagueis lean overall. Krayt takes sabers.
- For Krayt: on-page work against a top-tier entity. He punched into Abeloth, held through her Force blast, and drained both Luke and Abeloth: «The Sith seemed to be growing stronger as Abeloth grew weaker» (FotJ: Apocalypse). Insider #113: TK and lightning «far outstripped those of any Sith of his era». Reborn: «I have returned with my power multiplied» (Legacy: War). Dark Transfer. A master duelist, though young Hett lost to Obi-Wan (Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi).
- For Plagueis: Lucas-level film framing, near-equal-to-or-above-Sidious statements, absorbing blaster bolts into lightning, life/death mastery (Darth Plagueis). Plagueis has no fight with a top-tier opponent at all; Krayt does (Abeloth, with Luke).
- Krayt's minuses: he lost to Wyyrlok's poison plus Muur's lightning; he was ill for most of Legacy.
- What could flip it: if Krayt's Abeloth showing outranks Plagueis's statement-heavy case, it goes to Krayt. Forum (CV 1721047, opinion): mostly Plagueis, with Krayt taking sabers.

### Krayt vs Sidious (prime) (2026-10-11). Confidence: medium, Sidious
- Verdict: Sidious. The SI thread (debates-krayt-vs-sidious.md) went heavily Krayt, but no poster cited a feat, so it carries little weight. Sidious's on-page Council and Yoda results and his DE storms beat Krayt's showings, and Krayt's own hype tops out at "any Sith of his era".
- What could flip it: Krayt's Abeloth drain read as above Yoda-level.

### Panel ID owed to [member] (Krayt?) (2026-10-11). Status: CAN'T VERIFY without the source
- The fan image/thumbnail was never sourced. To check, Krayt's look: a heavily tattooed face, Vonduun crab armor grown over his body (New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology: it can deflect lightsabers), a double-bladed or single red saber.
