### Yoda (ROTS) vs Sidious (ROTS), neutral ground, all out (2026-10-12; updated 2026-10-19 with the ROTS novel and LoE). Winner: Sidious. Diff: high. Confidence: medium
- Versions: both at their ROTS state (19 BBY). That is the peak by default for Yoda. Sidious is post-Plagueis boost, without the Dark Empire amp. Amps: none, apart from the Order 66 dark-side context discussed below.
- Verdict: Sidious wins more often than not. It's close, and the fight result makes the gap look bigger than it is. Yoda is the better duelist. Sidious has the better offensive Force tool (lightning) and the deeper reserves on that day.
- The fight (ROTS film, script, JN, Stover novel). For Yoda: he Force-pushes Sidious over the desk. He drives him back in the office on neutral ground: «He drove Palpatine back across the room, into the Chancellor's podium» (ROTS JN), «PALPATINE seeks refuge in the vast Senate Chamber» (ROTS script). He disarms him: «the red lightsaber spun out of his hands and over the edge» (JN). In the script's first lightning clash «It looks as if the Dark Lord is doomed». For Sidious: lightning stops the killing blow, and the final clash ends with Yoda falling. JN: «until neither of them could hold it any longer». JN: «Never had Yoda faced one so strong in the dark side». Stover: «the creature had reached the limits of his strength... Half a second too slow» (ROTS novel, Ch20, L8453).
- Statements. Pro-Sidious (the majority): «Palpatine is too strong for the aging Yoda» (Comics Companion); «in the end the Sith bested him» (Complete SW Encyclopedia); the Insider #86 animators' framing that Yoda «has met his match»; Sidious's boast «Nor could Yoda» (Purge). Pro-equal: «matched every blow by Yoda's calm, measured skill» (Beware of the Sith); «just as powerful as Darth Sidious» (Mysteries of the Jedi, era not verified); «the ascendant dark side has made Sidious stronger» (Star Wars in 100 Scenes, a scan quoted on SI, says the edge is situational). Full lists: yoda-comicvine-respect.txt, sidious-comicvine-respect.txt, debates-yoda-mace-sidious.md. Labyrinth of Evil (added 2026-10-19): Dooku, who knew both, says Sidious's foresight «was one of the skills that distinguished Sidious from Yoda» (LoE, Ch39, L4193); Yoda's own POV: «This was Sidious: powerful enough to hide in plain sight.» (LoE, Ch39, L4245). That supports Sidious on preparation and information, not on raw power.
- Stover's beats (added 2026-10-19, ROTS novel, Ch20): Yoda redirects the opening lightning onto the Red Guards (L8301); Sidious scorches him; Yoda «rocketed from its huddle» and floors Sidious (L8311); blades and hand-to-hand are traded; the end is endurance plus an overcommitted leap («Half a second too slow», L8453); afterwards Sidious is «a very old, very tired man, gasping for air» (L8459). Yoda leaves for strategic reasons: «if he fell here, that hope would die with him» (L8411). Ch21 reframes the loss as one of method: «Too old I was,» Yoda said. «Too rigid.» (Ch21, L8641).
- Source check (2026-10-19): the JN disarm and the podium push cited above are NOT in Stover's text. Stover replaces them with the Red Guard redirect and the rocket counter. The net read is unchanged.
- Framing and intent: Lucas needed Yoda to lose but staged it close. Stover frames the loss as Yoda realizing the Jedi way itself had failed («just-didn't-have it... He had lost before he was born»). That is framing in Sidious's favor, but it's about the Order's approach as much as raw power. I weight it with the result, not above it.
- Environment: I don't give the podium excuse much weight. Sidious chose that ground, and being light is part of being Yoda. The reinforcement reason for leaving is real («he would summon his clone troops immediately», JN), and that's why this isn't high confidence.
- Common opponents: Dooku doesn't separate them (Yoda beat him twice; Sidious is his master). Mace: both rank above him (see below). Sidious beat Mace with Anakin's help, and Yoda is stated above Mace without any.
- What could flip it: a neutral-Force setting (no Order 66 surge; 100 Scenes / DarthAnt66 reading) moves it to a toss-up. Reading the script's lightning clash as the real flow gives Yoda the edge. A sabers-only rule set gives Yoda the edge (my view, which matches the SI t536 consensus).
- Forum (SI t205, opinion): about 10 posters say Sidious, about 4 say equal or Yoda. I agree with the result, not with the forum's "Yoda's saber edge doesn't matter". It matters, which is why this is high diff and not mid.

### Yoda (ROTS) vs Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad allowed) (2026-10-12; ROTS-novel cite added 2026-10-19). Winner: Yoda. Diff: mid-high. Confidence: medium-high
- Versions: Yoda at ROTS (peak). Mace at ROTS with Vaapad (amp included; against Yoda only his own-darkness Vaapad applies, see below).
- Verdict: Yoda. This has the cleanest statement chain of any PT pair, and Mace himself is on record.
- Statements: Mace: «Master Yoda is many things, and I am not his equal in peace or war» (Yoda: Dark Rendezvous). Mace's POV: «Mace was much less confident in his own raw power» than Yoda's (Shatterpoint). «only two opponents ever overcame him in battle. One was Master Yoda» and Mace «was still but a Padawan compared to Master Yoda» (Power of the Jedi Sourcebook). «Yoda's skill with a lightsaber was still second to none on the council» (Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter). «second most powerful Jedi on the that council, next to Yoda» (Insider #55). Gillard (creator): «second only to Yoda».
- Counter-statements: «powers on a par with those of the venerable Yoda» (Fact File remake #008, 2014, borderline Canon era). TPM-era pairings (TPM novel, Jedi Quest) rank both at the top, not as equals. PotJ SB «Perhaps only Master Mace Windu equaled him in skill and reputation» comes from the same book that says Yoda beat him.
- Vaapad (inferred from the ROTS novel's mechanics, and confirmed by the line-by-line read: Vaapad «drew the shadow's rage and power into his inmost center», ROTS novel, Ch17, L6691): the office-level amp loops the opponent's darkness («drew the shadow's rage and power into his inmost center... darkness flowed both ways»). Yoda gives him no dark-side power to loop, so Mace gets own-darkness Vaapad, not the «superconducting loop». Vaapad-allowed doesn't mean the office version here.
- Common opponents: Dooku. Yoda beat him twice and drove him off (AOTC: Dooku «held strong» but was pushed back; Vjun: «Slowly, slowly, Dooku gave way»). Mace had a brief even exchange (Republic: Obsession #5), needed Obi-Wan at Behpour (Wookieepedia), and lost to Dooku in sparring (PotJ SB). Sidious: both had strong showings. Mace's needed the Vaapad loop plus the Anakin shatterpoint. Yoda's didn't.
- What could flip it: treating Fact File #008 as authoritative; a long fight where Yoda's age and stamina matter (Shadow Hunter: «slowed slightly»); Vaapad's own-darkness amp being bigger than I'm assuming.

### Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad) vs Sidious (ROTS), office, no Anakin (2026-10-12; revised 2026-10-19 after the ROTS novel and LoE). Winner: Sidious. Diff: mid-high. Confidence: medium-high (was medium)
- Versions: Mace at ROTS with Vaapad and shatterpoint sense (amps included; this is his ceiling). Sidious at ROTS, post-Plagueis boost, no Dark Empire amp.
- Verdict: Sidious. Mace equals him with the blade only at Vaapad's ceiling, and loses the Force exchange.
- Sabers: the novel calls it a true stalemate: «no wound taken on either side, not even the possibility of fatigue. Impasse. Which might have gone on forever» (ROTS novel, Ch17, L6701–6703). The disarm came through a shatterpoint that was Anakin: «He had been so intent on Palpatine's shatterpoint that he'd never thought to look for Anakin's»; «Do you think the fear you feel is mine?» (ROTS novel). The film puts Anakin's arrival after the disarm, which supports a legit disarm (SI t313, PeraltaEagle45). The novel does not: Anakin is already at the door when Mace reads the shatterpoint (ROTS novel, Ch17, L6711–6713), and the ledge disarm (L6725) comes after that. So the novel is against the film-based "legit disarm before Anakin" reading. That is why confidence goes up to medium-high.
- Lightning: Mace's POV, «This was beyond Vaapad; he had no strength left to fight against his own blade» (ROTS novel, Ch17, L6773), and «Anakin, he's too strong for me-» (L6779). Both come before Sidious fakes the surrender (L6783–6785). Throughout, Sidious «was not afraid. Mace could feel it: he wasn't worried at all» (L6759). The film is more even. Sidious killed Kolar, Tiin and Fisto in seconds (both media).
- Amp and Anakin context: fighting Sidious is Vaapad's best case (the most darkness to channel), so this is Mace's ceiling. Take Anakin out and the novel's disarm opening is gone. The impasse holds until Sidious switches to lightning, which Mace can redirect but not outlast.
- Transitive check: Yoda > Mace and Sidious ≥ Yoda give Sidious > Mace. It's consistent.
- Labyrinth of Evil context (added 2026-10-19): Sidious hides from Mace face-to-face (LoE, Ch23, Ch31), and the Jedi miss a clouded clue: «How did we miss seeing this?» / «The answer is in the question.» (LoE, Ch34, L3773–3777). This supports Sidious choosing the time and ground. No change to the call.
- What could flip it: a film-purist reading (legit disarm, lightning held) gets close to a toss-up. Sabers-only rules make it a coin flip.
- Forum (SI t313, opinion): near consensus that Mace = Sidious in sabers while amped and Sidious > Mace in the Force. I reached this on the novel's own wording, not on the forum count.

### Yoda (Clone Wars era) vs Dooku (2026-10-17, after Dooku's DEEP pass; LoE statements added 2026-10-19). Winner: Yoda. Diff: mid. Confidence: high
- Versions: Yoda and Dooku as of the Clone Wars (22–19 BBY; Geonosis and Vjun). Peak Clone Wars versions; no amps (Dooku on a dark-side site is the flip case below).
- Verdict: Yoda. Dooku is close enough to hurt him and smart enough to always escape, but in a straight fight he loses.
- Fights: Geonosis, the AOTC novelization has Yoda's blade "forcing Dooku back" in the bladelock, and Dooku leaves by dropping a crane on Obi-Wan and Anakin. Vjun (Yoda: Dark Rendezvous) is the fair rematch: Dooku tags Yoda twice, once off a distraction, then in a straight exchange "Slowly, slowly, Dooku gave way," and Dooku admits "There was always a chance you could overpower me" before running behind a falling missile.
- Statements: Lucas (AOTC commentary) and the AOTC diorama ("near equal strength in the Force") make them equal in the Force at Geonosis. Fact File #34 (Relaunched): "almost equals, with... Yoda having perhaps a slight edge." Dooku himself says the Force can't decide it (AOTC). So the Force is close, and the blade is where Yoda pulls ahead. Labyrinth of Evil (added 2026-10-19), Dooku's own POV: «On Geonosis, Yoda's easy parrying and, indeed, handling of the Sith lightning Dooku hurled at him had come as a surprise» (LoE, Ch26, L2451), an admission against interest. Yoda learned the new Sith's danger only by fighting him: «He hadn't had a sense of that danger until he had fought Dooku on Geonosis.» (LoE, Ch39, L4243). Dooku's counter-claim that he «had only fled the fight to safeguard the plans» (L2451) is face-saving and weighted low. Net: slightly strengthened.
- Narrative: both duels are written as Dooku avoiding a decision he'd lose. That's author intent pointing at Yoda.
- What could flip it: Dooku wins by tactics (hostages, traps, a feigned-weakness lightning ambush shown only as an image in the respect thread, source unverified). Yoda holding back out of love (Dark Rendezvous) cuts the other way.

### Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad) vs Dooku (ROTS) (2026-10-17; LoE and ROTS-novel evidence added 2026-10-19). Winner: Mace. Diff: high. Confidence: low-medium
- Versions: Mace at ROTS with Vaapad (amp included). Dooku at ROTS (19 BBY). Peak versions for both.
- Verdict: Mace on neutral ground. Dooku on a dark-side site like Vjun makes it a coin flip.
- For Dooku: Power of the Jedi Sourcebook says only Yoda and Dooku "ever overcame" Mace (sparring, Jedi era). TCW Lightsaber Duels: "You were never able to defeat me at the Jedi Temple." Dark Rendezvous (Yoda's view): "Among the other Jedi, perhaps only Mace Windu would have been his equal on neutral ground."
- For Mace: the Temple spars were before Vaapad was finished (Mace refined it through Shatterpoint and after). At Behpour (Wookieepedia, Dooku/Legends), Obi-Wan and Mace together beat him, though that was 2-on-1. ROTS Mace held ROTS Sidious to a sword stalemate (ROTS novel: "Impasse"), which nothing in Dooku's record matches. Reference books later rate Mace and Yoda as the two who "eclipsed" him (Starships & Vehicles #48).
- For Mace (added 2026-10-19): Dooku's own ladder, to Grievous: «Do I need to demonstrate what responses you can expect from Cin Drallig or Obi-Wan Kenobi? From Mace Windu or, stars help you, Yoda?» (LoE, Ch32, L3347), which puts Mace just under Yoda. Grievous: «Tyranus had warned him about Mace Windu's prowess with a blade, and now he understood.» (LoE, Ch50, L4929). The ROTS novel confirms that Vaapad feeds on the opponent's darkness: it «drew the shadow's rage and power into his inmost center» (ROTS novel, Ch17, L6691), and Dooku has plenty. The ROTS novel has no direct Mace–Dooku data: Mace's «I have fought him blade-to-blade» (Ch10, L3413) is about Grievous.
- Confidence kept at low-medium: LoE's worker called medium defensible, the ROTS worker called it only mild support, and neither book has a Mace–Dooku fight.
- Common opponents: Sidious (Mace stalemates him with the blade; Dooku is his apprentice and Sidious calls him a pawn). Anakin (beat Dooku on the Invisible Hand; Mace isn't rated below Anakin anywhere).
- What could flip it: weight the sparring record and "equal on neutral ground" over the Sidious duel, and it's a toss-up. Vaapad needs a dark opponent to feed on, and Dooku is one, so that point favors Mace.

### Dooku (AOTC to ROTS) vs Darth Maul (TPM, Legends) (2026-10-17; Darth Plagueis cites added 2026-10-19). Winner: Dooku. Diff: mid. Confidence: medium
- Versions: Dooku at his AOTC–ROTS peak; Maul at TPM (Legends). No amps.
- Verdict: Dooku, mostly early. The longer it goes, the better Maul's odds.
- Statements: Insider #69: "Count Dooku is more skillful than Maul... Dooku countered Kenobi's moves almost effortlessly because he knew precisely where to block." Panel-to-Panel Vol 1: "if anything deadlier than Maul." Legacy of the Jedi: Obi-Wan "had never come up against something that had completely overpowered him. Even meeting the Sith Lord who had killed Qui-Gon had not been the same." Labyrinth of Evil: Sidious saw Maul as "nothing more than a minion," and Dooku as "an equal from the other camp."
- Counter-statements: Maul's prowess "may have been second only" to Sidious (Shadow Hunter / Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels, TPM era, with a "perhaps"). Gillard (out-of-universe) rates both as 8.
- Common opponent, Obi-Wan: TPM Obi-Wan (a Padawan) killed Maul after Maul beat Qui-Gon. AOTC Obi-Wan (a Knight, ten years better) was "completely overpowered" by Dooku, who also beat him again on the Invisible Hand. That's a rough Dooku lean.
- Maul's best counter-evidence (added after reading Erkan12's Maul RT, same day): The Dark Side Sourcebook says he "nearly bested his master... Sidious barely deflected them all" in his final test, and Sidious calls his swordsmanship "peerless" (Saboteur). But the Darth Plagueis novel, the newer and stronger source, tells the same test as Sidious disarming him ("he fought well, even after I deprived him of his lightsaber"). Common opponent: both beat Komari Vosa (Maul while wounded, Lockdown). It doesn't separate them.
- Darth Plagueis (added 2026-10-19; TPM-era Maul): Plagueis tells Sidious «you allowed him to believe that he is more skilled than he actually is» (Darth Plagueis, Ch23, L5215). On the Black Sun mission a lightly Force-sensitive gangster wounds him: «the Black Sun leader cut open your hand» (Ch28, L6441). Both lean Dooku.
- What could flip it: stamina. Wookieepedia lists Dooku's age and stamina as liabilities in long fights, and Maul is a relentless pressure fighter, which is the style that troubles Makashi. The Canon list that puts TPM Maul above ROTS Tyranus is a separate continuity (Canon note only).
- SI (opinion): t2957 split with a slight Maul lean; t2531 (SoD Maul, composite) leaned Dooku.

### Darth Vader vs Dooku (ROTS), split by Vader version (2026-10-17; split 2026-10-19 after the ROTS novel and LoE). Unsuited Mustafar Vader: Vader, mid diff, medium-high. Newly suited Vader (end of ROTS): toss-up, slight Dooku lean, high diff, low. Later suited prime (ROTJ/comics): Vader, mid-high diff, low-medium
- Versions: Dooku = 19 BBY (ROTS, age 83). Vader is split per the house rule, on the ROTS novel's narration to the newly suited Vader: «you are so far less now than what you were, you are more than half machine» … «the power you can touch is only a memory» (ROTS novel, Ch21, L8867). (1) Unsuited Mustafar Vader (newly turned, 19 BBY) is the peak Vader and the default. (2) Suited Vader starts with the newly suited Vader at the end of ROTS, which is what L8867 describes. (3) The later suited prime (ROTJ/comics) is listed separately, because L8867 was written about the newly suited Vader. Amps: none counted beyond the rage that is part of Mustafar Vader.
- Verdict (unsuited Mustafar Vader): Vader, in a real fight, not a stomp.
- Reasoning: Anakin already beat Dooku on the Invisible Hand by switching to raw aggression and power (ROTS novel, Ch4, L1601: «Dooku's decades of combat experience are irrelevant. His mastery of swordplay is useless.»; Wookieepedia: "overwhelmed Dooku's defenses"). That feat belongs to pre-fall, rage-amped Anakin (see the Dooku vs Anakin entry below). Mustafar Vader keeps that strength and Form V pressure, and he has Anakin's memory of how Dooku fights. Dark Lord (Luceno): Dooku was one of only three ever good enough with a blade to injure Vader, so the Count does trouble him.
- For Dooku: better technique and Makashi, instructor-level knowledge of every form, a long record of handling bigger and stronger opponents (Grievous spars, Labyrinth of Evil, though LoE says Dooku was at times «hard-pressed to outduel the cyborg» and «had kept some secrets to himself», LoE, Ch22, L1669–1671; his on-page demo is a Makashi disarm of two MagnaGuards with the tip at Grievous's face, LoE, Ch32, L3349). Before Anakin's rage turn, the Invisible Hand duel went his way for a while. In the ROTS novel Dooku was holding back and tiring before Anakin's rage took hold, so nothing argues for a bigger margin.
- Suited Vader: per L8867, the newly suited Vader of late ROTS is well below Mustafar Vader, so the Ch4 and Mustafar feats overrate him. Against Dooku that version is even or leans Dooku (high diff, low confidence). The later suited prime (ROTJ/comics) keeps the old Vader lean at mid-high diff, but confidence drops to low-medium: the old merged entry rested mainly on Anakin's Invisible Hand win, which counts for pre-fall Anakin, not for suited Vader.
- What could flip it: sabers-only and no prior knowledge (BreakofDawn on SI argues Dooku wins sabers then). The early stiff-suit Vader (Dark Lord era) is worse than Mustafar Anakin.
- SI (opinion): t472 big Vader majority; t187 sabers-only split with a Vader lean.

### Darth Sidious vs Dooku (2026-10-17; LoE and ROTS-novel cites added 2026-10-19). Winner: Sidious. Diff: low-mid. Confidence: high
- Versions: Sidious at ROTS (19 BBY, post-Plagueis boost, no Dark Empire amp); Dooku at 19 BBY. Peak versions.
- Labyrinth/ROTS framing: Dooku perceives Palpatine as "an event horizon... A black hole of the Force" (ROTS novel, Ch3, L1351–1353); Sidious keeps Dooku as a disposable pawn and has him killed. Dooku himself thinks «Lord Sidious could come up with a new plan more easily than a new apprentice» (ROTS novel, Ch3, L1505), and Sidious says «Dooku was not lost, he was sacrificed» (Ch10, L3509). Dooku never wins a duel against anyone Sidious-tier.
- Labyrinth of Evil (added 2026-10-19): Dooku's dark-side training was «a crash course in tapping into the power of the dark side - - a mere taste of which had proved intoxicating» (LoE, Ch26, L2445). Yoda: «Hard to know if Dooku a true Sith is, or simply with the power of the dark side infatuated.» (LoE, Ch31, L3299). Sidious scripts the Invisible Hand duel: «Should he by some fluke best you, however, I will control the outcome to spare you any unnecessary embarrassment» (LoE, Ch55, L5261).
- Diff wording: LoE's worker said low, ROTS's worker said low-to-mid. Recorded as low-mid.

### Character-backfill head-to-heads (2026-10-17, from the per-book "Character analyses" sections). All primary-source (novel line numbers), except where marked.

#### Mara Jade Skywalker vs Lumiya, one-on-one (40 ABY). Confidence: medium, Mara
- Verdict: Mara wins a fair 1v1.
- Reasoning: on Hesperidium (Sacrifice Ch10) Mara lands every clean blow: a five-meter Force leap, a blaster hit to the shoulder, and the hilt-dagger stab through Lumiya's chest (L5248–5258). She was stopped only when the Sith sphere ambushed her from behind (L5268; «I got bushwhacked by a living ship», L6816). Lumiya was on a decoy mission (L3940). Tempest Ch6 adds that a Council Master (Lobi) was «slowly forcing Lumiya back» 1v1 (Tempest L1668).
- What could flip it: Lumiya fighting to win from a prepared position (her phantom and possession techniques, Exile Ch10). Lumiya was not trying to win either time.

#### Darth Caedus vs Kyle Katarn (Fury era). Confidence: high, Caedus
- Verdict: Caedus, quickly.
- Reasoning: Fury Ch10–11. Katarn led a four-Jedi ambush with gas and dazzle grenades. Caedus, still recovering from Inferno (L1715), downed three Knights in «Two seconds» (L1577) and ran Katarn through with a speeder-yank feint (L1649), then beheaded Mithric (L1723). Caedus's private read was «Katarn, though, was a threat.» (L1571), so Katarn was respected.
- Caveat: Katarn went down to a trick, not a saber exchange. Katarn himself is still INTRO tier in the tracker beyond this book.

#### Darth Caedus vs Saba Sebatyne (Fury era). Confidence: medium, Caedus
- Reasoning: Caedus's private assessment: «Saba, with difficulty. Saba plus Luke would be impossible odds.» (Fury L5993–5995). On the bridge he removed her with opportunistic TK while she was deflecting cannon fire (L6629–6633), and she still stood back up (L6711). No clean 1v1.

#### Leia Organa Solo vs Tahiri Veila (Inferno), and Ben Skywalker vs Tahiri (Invincible). Confidence: medium, Leia; medium, Ben
- Leia was beating down Tahiri's guard with Barabel-style strikes (Inferno L4475). Tahiri landed only when Han distracted Leia (L4481). Ben beat Tahiri in the falling duel and chose to parry instead of killing her (LotF 9 L5412–5430), though Tahiri did not want to win (L5430).

#### Darth Malgus vs Aryn Leneer (Deceived). Confidence: high, Malgus
- Duel 1 (Ch11) was inconclusive: Aryn landed the only clean wound (L6157) and left by choice. Duel 2 (Ch13): Malgus wins decisively. His lightning, used «almost casually», «exceeded anything she had felt from Malgus before» (L7015) and broke her guard. He spared her to repay a debt (L7143). Duel 1 understates his ceiling.

#### Darth Malgus vs Ven Zallow (Deceived). Confidence: medium-high, Malgus
- In the blade lock «neither had an obvious advantage» (L897). Malgus won on a feint (L915–921), and Aryn's reading of the footage confirms the bait (L5713). Close in raw power; Malgus ahead in tactics. Chain from the same book: Malgus > Zallow > Adraas (L873).

#### Darth Vader (Dark Lord, 19 BBY) vs Roan Shryne / Bol Chatak / Jedi Knights. Confidence: high, Vader
- Even at his worst (Murkhana), Vader beats Chatak on power, though her cut shook him (L1315–1319). By Kashyyyk he is «Toying with the Jedi» (L4807) against Forte and Kulka 2v1, and he kills Shryne after the book's longest duel. Shryne landed three hits, all on prosthetics (L4989, L4995, L5141). This sets early-Vader's floor above elite Knights. It changes nothing in Vader vs Dooku/Revan/Malgus.

#### Tier impact
- **No tier changes.** The backfill confirms the existing tier-5 placement of Luke > Caedus and the LotF ladders. New supporting order for the LotF era, below Caedus: Saba ≳ Katarn (Master tier) > Jaina (top Knight until Invincible) > Mara 1v1 ≥ Lumiya > Alema; Leia > Tahiri (Inferno); Ben ≥ Tahiri (Invincible). Malgus stays where his debates files put him. Deceived only adds Aryn and Zallow as calibration below him.
- Change log: 2026-10-17 (character backfill). Seven new SW head-to-heads above. No tier moves.

### Exar Kun / Sion DEEP pass + Caedus vs Krayt (2026-10-18 study)
### Exar Kun vs Count Dooku (ROTS era) (2026-10-18). Confidence: medium, Kun (about 6.5/10)
- Verdict: Kun. Dooku is the better pure fencer on paper, but Kun's Force and sorcery ceiling is a tier above, and his dueling record is elite.
- Fights / feats: Kun = Ulic Qel-Droma on blades, "too evenly matched for either to gain the upper hand. Their battle might have gone on for hours" (Dark Side Sourcebook; DLotS #6). Kills Vodo-Siosk Baas, a recognized weapon master, once the saberstaff comes out (Sith War #3; Power of the Jedi Sourcebook: "no match for Exar Kun's double-bladed lightsaber and deep reserve of dark side power"), while holding a spell over the Senate and then dominating Chancellor Sidrona's mind. Odan-Urr's Force strike and sever attempt only knock him back (Sith War #1). Obliterates Freedon Nadd's spirit (amulet-boosted, DLotS #4). Dooku's best: holds off Obi-Wan + Anakin (ROTS), near-equal Force exchange with Yoda on Geonosis, loses the fair blade exchange to Yoda on Vjun ("Slowly, slowly, Dooku gave way").
- Statements: Jedi Academy Sourcebook: "Kun was far more powerful than any one other Jedi of the time" (an era of the strong old Jedi; Odan-Urr, Thon, Nomi). Weapons & Technology: "virtually unstoppable in combat". Complete SW Encyclopedia: "the most powerful and dangerous of the Dark Lords" to his era. For Dooku: "Only Masters Yoda and Mace Windu were considered to be on equal terms with him" (Insider #109).
- Narrative framing: Kun is the main villain of a war that wrecked a quarter of the Republic's civilized worlds and needed the whole Order to stop him; Dooku is explicitly Sidious's disposable second.
- Common opponents / links: none direct. Indirect: Kun = Ulic (who later beat Mandalore the Indomitable and fought Nomi's whole Order - INTRO tier for Ulic). Dooku ~ just under Yoda/Mace. Spirit Kun + Kyp overwhelmed ~11 ABY Luke (Dark Apprentice), but 2-on-1, Luke defending only.
- What could flip it: a pure-sabers round (Dooku's Makashi vs a strength-based Niman variant could go Dooku); counting the Malak quote at face value plus Malak ~ Dooku ideas; a ruling that Kun's big Force feats are all amulet- or nexus-dependent (the Nadd kill and Corsair lift were on Yavin with the amulet).
- SI (opinion): t22 went Dooku ~9-3. I disagree: the Dooku side argued against AncientPower's chains, not against Kun's own feats. t4525 SS was never posted.

### Exar Kun vs Revan (SoR / Revan Reborn) (2026-10-18; Revan-novel feats added 2026-10-19). Winner: Revan (Revan Reborn version), slight. Diff: high. Confidence: low-medium (was low)
- Versions: Revan = Revan Reborn (the Revan novel's peak, 3,951 BBY, balanced «on the knife-edge», Revan, Ch27, L5803), no amp. Kun = living Sith War Kun. His amulet- and Yavin-nexus-dependent feats are included but flagged (see "What could flip it"). The Star Forge win cited below belongs to KOTOR 1 end Revan (Jedi, light-side route). It carries to Revan Reborn only as a floor, and nobody who knew both versions compares them directly.
- Revan novel (added 2026-10-19; counts for Revan Reborn only): a one-exchange lightning-absorb kill of a Dark Councilor (Revan, Ch24, L5419–5425: Nyriss is left as «a pile of charred ash») and a competitive opening against the base Emperor before he loses (Ch28, L5987, L5995). These are new Reborn-version feats beyond KOTOR, so confidence moves from low to low-medium. The diff stays high.
- Verdict: Revan by a hair overall. Kun likely takes a Force-only round (sorcery); all-out is close.
- Fights / feats: Revan beat Malak on the Star Forge while Malak drained the captive Jedi ("You cannot beat me, Revan. Not here on the Star Forge", KOTOR); Revan's longer arc and the Vitiate captivity show he fights top-tier entities and survives. Kun's record (Ulic parity, Baas, Odan-Urr, Nadd's spirit, Senate spell) is strong but against a lower ceiling of opponents than Star Forge Malak.
- Statements: WotC "Darth Malak: An Expanded Universe Character": "Did it provide him with powers far greater than even Exar Kun or Freedon Nadd?" (a question, and the author later reportedly said it meant Star Forge/galactic power; disputed). It's weak but it's the only direct statement, and it points to Revan's side via Malak. Against: KOTOR II Nadd-tomb lines ("far worse than Revan and Malak ever were") are cut-content companion dialogue and may mean "more evil".
- Narrative framing: both are their era's archetypal fallen-Jedi Dark Lord; Kun needed the united Order to stop him, Revan was stopped by a Jedi strike team and then rebuilt and beat Malak.
- Common links: Kun and Revan both connect to Malachor/Sith teachings; Sion fought in Kun's army and later trained at Revan's academy (no power link). No shared opponent.
- What could flip it: dropping the Malak quote entirely (then Kun's sorcery + saberstaff edge makes it a toss-up or Kun); treating Revan Reborn's SWTOR growth as big (Revan up).
- SI (opinion): t3417 Revan ~7-3; BreakofDawn 2021 split by round (Revan sabers, Kun Force/all-out).

### Exar Kun vs Darth Vader (ROTJ / suit prime) (2026-10-18). Confidence: medium, Kun (about 6/10)
- (Picked over Maul: t29 has more argued evidence than the Maul threads, which posted no quotes.)
- Verdict: Kun more often than not.
- Reasoning: Vader's suit caps his mobility and Force ceiling (the standard Legends reading of post-ROTS Vader); his ROTJ fight with Luke is a near-equal duel ("a battle of equals", ROTJ comic adaptation). Kun's sorcery (Senate-wide spell, mind domination, Sith-spirit crystal corruption) gives him a win condition Vader has never had to answer, and on blades he is Ulic's equal and built a style around tricking opponents (Weapons & Technology). Spirit Kun + Kyp also beat ~11 ABY Luke, who per I, Jedi was "redoubled" after Dark Empire, i.e. above ROTJ Luke (2-on-1 caveat).
- Statements: Luke ranks Kun with Palpatine as "two of the greatest focal points of the dark side he'd ever had to face" (Specter of the Past), never Vader in that pair.
- What could flip it: using peak Mustafar-era / Dark Lord-era Vader (closer); counting Malak quote + Malak ~ Vader; Kun's big feats being nexus-assisted.
- Maul note: Kun > Maul all-out (medium); Maul may edge sabers (low). SI t820/t1853 agree by round.
- SI (opinion): t29 Kun ~7-3.

### Darth Sion vs Darth Nihilus (KOTOR II era) (2026-10-18). Confidence: medium-high, Nihilus (about 8/10)
- Verdict: Nihilus wins, meaning he defeats/neutralizes Sion; he may not make him stay dead unless his drain targets what holds Sion together.
- Reasoning: In the betrayal of Traya, Nihilus does the decisive work: "Nihilus used his dark variant of the Sever Force ability to betray Darth Traya alongside Darth Sion by stripping her of the Force" (Wookieepedia Nihilus); Sion "larruped her into submission" after Nihilus Force-pushed her. The SWTOR Codex lists Nihilus first ("whose hunger devoured all life around him"). Kreia's framing in KOTOR II makes Nihilus the greater danger (a wound in the Force that consumes worlds, e.g. Katarr) and Sion a lord who learned only pain ("Of knowledge, of teaching, he knows nothing").
- Fight: the only direct one is CUT content (Ravager): Nihilus's wave blasts Sion back and kills soldiers; Sion survives and walks off "disgusted". Low weight, but it shows Nihilus hitting and Sion only enduring.
- Common opponents: the Exile beats both. Sion falls 4+ times and is talked into dying; Nihilus needs the Exile + Visas (+ Mandalore) and the Exile's Force-bond trait is his specific counter, so the Exile result flatters Sion relative to Nihilus.
- What could flip it: if the cut scene is read as Sion no-selling Nihilus and Sion's immortality is unlimited on a nexus; if "win" requires permanent death and Nihilus's drain can't sever the dark-side binding.
- SI (opinion): no Sion vs Nihilus thread exists. AncientPower uses the cut scene for Sion; Romeothekotorlover reads it as Nihilus one-shotting him.

### Darth Sion vs Meetra Surik (the Exile, Malachor V) (2026-10-18). Confidence: high, the Exile (about 9/10)
- Verdict: the Exile. This is what actually happened.
- Reasoning: Korriban: she fights him and wounds him; he heals and lets her go (Kreia had told her to flee). Malachor V: she strikes him down at least four times, and on the last she breaks his will (he admits his feelings for her, she shows him Kreia is using him) and he lets himself die ("I am glad to leave this place…at last."). The game frames her as his conqueror both physically and mentally. Prima guide: "Darth Sion heals at will, but you can win by striking him down repeatedly."
- Caveats: Early-game (Peragus/Korriban) Exile was much weaker and Sion was "unbeatable" at her then strength (Kreia). Version matters: early Exile vs Sion on Korriban = Sion.
- What could flip it: only a pre-Malachor Exile, or rules that stop her from talking.

### Darth Sion vs Darth Maul (TPM, Legends) (2026-10-18). Confidence: low-medium, Maul (about 6/10)
- (Picked over Vader as the closer and more useful matchup. Vader vs Sion: Vader, high, ~8.5/10. Vader's power, skill and the "nowhere near Vader level" consensus all line up, and Sion has no answer to Vader's TK/choke beyond getting up again.)
- Verdict: Maul wins most fights under standard rules (incapacitate or kill), but it's a grind, not a stomp.
- Reasoning: On blades Maul is clearly better: he nearly beat Sidious in his final test (Dark Side Sourcebook), killed Qui-Gon, and fights Dooku close. Sion's combat record is thin (wins over a weakened Kreia and a trapped Vash; repeatedly beaten by the Exile). Maul can put him down repeatedly. Sion's case is pure attrition: he heals at will and rises, and on Korriban/Malachor he says "I cannot be killed". Maul is relentless and has great stamina, but he has no mind-game to make Sion let go, and he can't dismember the binding.
- Common opponents: none. Indirect: Exile > Sion (high), Vader > Exile (SI opinion, t1100; not my verdict), Dooku > Maul (6.5/10).
- What could flip it: fighting on a dark-side nexus with "win = permanent kill" makes it Sion by attrition (Maul runs out first). Neutral ground, where Sion's immortality may be weaker (SI t1424 debated this; unresolved), makes it Maul more clearly.

### Darth Caedus (Invincible era) vs Darth Krayt (2026-10-18). Confidence: medium-high, Krayt (about 7.5/10 for reborn Krayt; about 6.5/10 for FotJ-era Krayt)
- Correction note: replaces an earlier quick take, which was wrong. The tier list already had Krayt (tier 4) above Caedus (tier 5).
- Verdict: Krayt wins. Reborn Krayt (Legacy: War) wins clearly; FotJ-era Krayt (44 ABY, partly Vong-afflicted, the closest era match) still wins, but it's closer.
- Common opponent, Luke: Luke beats Caedus again and again (Inferno: Force-pins him and nearly kills him; Revelation Fondor: hides from his senses and cracks his chest; Invincible: wins the final duels; Caedus's own POV "Luke had beaten him"). Krayt fought next to Luke against Abeloth in FotJ: Apocalypse, Luke was "wary of dueling Krayt", and Krayt's drain harmed both Abeloth and Luke ("plundering the entity's Force energy while harming her and Luke Skywalker"). Luke's 40 ABY visions saw Krayt as "at least as ruthless and strong in the Force as the Chosen One". So Luke is clearly above Caedus and at best roughly level with Krayt.
- Feats: Krayt fought Abeloth beyond shadows (cut-off hand restored, yanked her back by recalling his embedded hand) and later, reborn: overpowers Cade "with mostly his usage of the Force alone", "practically vaporize[s]" temple pillars, kills and resurrects Cade by dark transfer, beats Wyyrlok's lightning bare-handed. Caedus's best: the Fondor shield drop by mass mind-influence (fed by fleet battle meditation), shatterpoint, flow-walking, Aing-Tii fighting-sight; he's drained by the big feats and admits «No, I am not omnipotent» (Revelation).
- Framing: Krayt is the head of the One Sith and the "One Sith" Tenebrous foresaw, built as an era-defining final boss; Caedus is a tragic fallen Jedi whose arc ends with Jaina killing him.
- What could flip it: Legacy-era sick Krayt (Vong coral eating him, lost to Wyyrlok's poison + Muur), where Caedus's tricks and breadth could win; Caedus pre-reading the fight with flow-walking. Neither is enough against reborn Krayt.
- Short version: "krayt takes it. luke beats caedus basically every time they fight, and the same luke was nervous about fighting krayt and got hurt by his drain in the abeloth fight, and that's before reborn krayt gets even stronger"

### KOTOR 1 + 2 walkthrough pass (2026-10-19). Source: StrategyWiki game walkthroughs (intermediate depth, transcribed game dialog, NOT the game itself). Notes: kotor-1-notes.md, kotor-2-notes.md
### Revan (KOTOR 1) vs Darth Malak (Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: high, Revan
- Verdict: Revan. This is what happens in the game, and Malak concedes it in his own words.
- Reasoning: Malak, before the final duel: «You are stronger than I thought; stronger than you ever were during your reign as the Dark Lord» (K1/Viewing_Platform). Dying, he says «You are the one who deserves... to be the Dark Lord... I only followed in your wake.» Vandar: «Revan was always the leader, the more powerful of the pair» (K1/Jedi_Enclave). Revan wins on the Star Forge even though Malak drains captive Jedi to fully restore himself («Not when I can draw upon the power of all these Jedi!»).
- Weak spots: on the Leviathan an early, underleveled Revan loses to Malak and is saved by Bastila (K1/Hangar). Malak's claims of having "surpassed" Revan are self-serving and come before the amnesia arc ends. The gameplay outcome depends on the player's build.
- What could flip it: only pre-Star-Forge amnesiac Revan vs Star-Forge-amped Malak.

### Darth Nihilus vs Darth Traya (Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: low, slight Nihilus lean for the fight; Traya for skill/knowledge
- Verdict: unchanged lean that Nihilus beats Traya in a direct clash. He (with Sion) already overthrew her, and Kreia herself says «There are techniques within the Force against which there is no defense. I was cast down. Stripped of my power.» (K2/Kreia). Traya is the more complete Force user.
- New wiki evidence for Traya: the final-boss kit (three floating lightsabers, the highest stats in the game) and the drain that kills Vrook, Kavar and Zez-Kai Ell together (K2/Rebuilt_Jedi_Enclave). Sion: «She... cannot be defeated.»
- New wiki evidence for Nihilus: incapacitates the whole party on sight (K2/Bridge); Katarr's death stated by the Masters and Atris; Atris calls him «the greatest of her apprentices» (K2/Telos).
- Weak spots: Kreia says his hunger is «not something he can direct or focus» and that it «devours him as he devours others». The betrayal scene itself is not on the wiki.

### Darth Nihilus vs the Exile (Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: medium, the Exile (in-game); low for a neutral rematch without Visas
- Verdict: the Exile wins, as in the game, but with help and a hard counter.
- Reasoning: Nihilus incapacitates the party. When he moves to drain the Exile he «suddenly reels back, collapsing». Visas's link disruption, or her sacrifice taking him to 20% Vitality, decides it (K2/Bridge). Traya: the Exile is «A dead spot in the Force», which is exactly what a drainer can't feed on.
- What could flip it: remove Visas and the bond mechanic, and Nihilus's planet-scale hunger is the bigger power. Keep low confidence for a neutral fight.

### Darth Sion vs the Exile, and Sion vs Traya (Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: high, the Exile (unchanged); medium-high, Traya
- Exile: the wiki confirms the existing entry. On Korriban, Sion «restores himself to maximum» and Kreia orders a retreat. On Malachor he must be beaten «four times» and ends with «You... have defeated me... flesh and belief, both cast down.» (K2/Sith_Academy, K2/Trayus_Academy_(Top)).
- Traya: Sion admits «She... cannot be defeated» and «if we were to challenge her, we would die». He also claims «And you have not bested her in battle, as I have» and severed her hand on the Harbinger, but against a stripped, weakened Kreia (K2/Engine_Deck). Later he concedes «I spared you once, I will not do so again» (K2/Malachor_V).
- New caveat: Sion's immortality is tied to place: «while Korriban runs through him» and «As long as the dark places of this world flow through the cracks of my flesh». That supports tier 7: immortality is a modifier, not raw power.

### Darth Traya vs the Exile (Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: medium-high, the Exile (endgame)
- Verdict: the Exile. This is what happens in the game, and Traya endorses it: «I have used you so that you might become strong, stronger than I» and «You are greater than any I have ever trained» (K2/Trayus_Core). Sion: «in time, you shall surpass her power».
- Weak spots: Traya engineered the fight as a test and wanted to lose. Early-game Exile is far below her.

### Revan vs the Exile / Revan vs the KOTOR 2 Lords (Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: low, no change
- The wiki adds hype but no new fights: «Only Revan was worthy of our respect» (Mandalore), «Only Revan ever demonstrated such skill in war» (Handmaiden), and HK-47's «subtle, intelligent cruelties» versus Malak, «more like an angry club». Kreia: «Revan's choices were always his own» and the "true Sith" lie beyond the Outer Rim. No new evidence on the Revan vs Nihilus/Traya/Exile power ranking. Keep current tier-5 placements.

### KOTOR deep pass addendum (Oct 19, 2026, second read). Strengthens existing entries; no flips
- Nihilus vs the Exile: strengthened, still medium. On the bridge the drain backfires before Visas acts at all: "Nihilus raises his hand to drain you, but suddenly reels back, collapsing on the ground". Visas's disruption only adds "incapacitated for one combat round" (narration, K2/Bridge). Traya: «no Jedi ever made the choice you did. To sever ties so completely, so utterly, that it leaves a wound in the Force» (K2/Trayus_Core). Atris: «You were strong enough to withstand it once - but few have your strength in such matters» (K2/Telos). The neutral-rematch lean moves from low to low-medium, the Exile, because the counter is innate to her rather than dependent on Visas.
- Traya: background confirmed as Revan's first teacher («At one time, Revan was my Padawan», K2/Kreia). Revan's later masters were «Zhar, Dorak, Master Kae» (K2/Enclave_Sublevel). Nihilus vs Traya stays low.
- Revan vs Sion: newly explicit. Sion himself says «I have come farther than any of her apprentices since Revan», which places Revan above him (K2/Trayus_Academy_(Top)). Kreia: «Revan was power. It was like staring into the heart of the Force.» (K2/Kreia). No tier change; this matches the current ordering.
- Atris vs the Exile (new, Oct 19, 2026). Confidence: medium-high, the Exile. The Exile defeats her on Telos (K2/Telos). She leaked the Exile's location to bait the Sith and drew on Sith holocrons. Traya: «I never destroyed Atris - she had destroyed herself» (K2/Trayus_Core).
- Revan vs Malak: strengthened, still high. The Viewing Platform page puts Malak's Attack as «may well be the highest in the entire game», and he regenerates by draining up to eight captive Jedi. Revan still wins, and Malak's own «Once you were stronger than me, Revan» (K1/Viewing_Platform) concedes Revan's original superiority.
- Restored Content Mod: checked; it contains no power-scaling scenes, so no verdict uses cut content.

### Tier impact (Oct 19, 2026)
- No tier moves. Revan > Malak (high) and Sion's tier 7 are confirmed. Malak is not yet placed: tentatively low tier 5 or high tier 6, below Revan (high). The Exile (Meetra) is tentatively tier 5, below Revan (low), above Sion (high) and Traya (medium-high, in-game). That placement is not official until her DEEP pass. Traya stays in tier 5 near Nihilus.

### DEEP pass: Malak, Exile, Luke, Maul + owed verdicts (2026-10-19 study)
Sources: malak-comicvine-respect.txt, meetra-comicvine-respect.txt, debates-malak-exile.md, luke-comicvine-respect.txt, debates-luke.md, debates-maul.md, debates-yoda-mace-sidious.md (t1259 section), plus the KOTOR notes and dossiers. SI posters are OPINION ONLY. All verdicts are Legends unless labeled. How the scale maps: low diff = about 8.5/10 or more; mid diff = about 6.5-8/10; high diff = about 5.5-6/10.

#### Darth Plagueis vs Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad), all-out, neutral (2026-10-19, requested by a member; Darth Plagueis cites added later 2026-10-19). Winner: Plagueis. Diff: mid-high. Confidence: low-medium
- Versions: Plagueis prime (Darth Plagueis Part Three, 33–32 BBY, including the permanent ~41 BBY shift amp). Mace at ROTS with Vaapad (amp included).
- Reasoning: Mace's best showing is a saber stalemate with ROTS Sidious, but he loses the all-out version (Sidious, mid-high diff; see the Mace vs Sidious entry). Plagueis has Sidious's breadth and more: midi-chlorian manipulation; the marionette technique that beat Venamis (working his own body «like a marionette», Darth Plagueis, Ch6, L1553); surviving two lightning barrages without defending himself, because they grounded on his transpirator, then raising a Force storm while suffocating (Ch30, L7219–7243; this is the drunk, dying Plagueis, so it's a durability floor, not a peak feat); and life/death sorcery.
- Dueling credential (added 2026-10-19): Tenebrous «had pronounced Plagueis a master of the art» (Ch6, L1547), and the Venamis duel was a mid-diff win with a hit taken («searing the side of Plagueis's neck», L1549; L1549–1561). Both are 67 BBY Plagueis, a floor for his prime. Mace takes a sabers-only round clearly (SI t1259 agrees). All-out, Plagueis's Force versatility and his willingness to fight from range decide it.
- Common opponents / indirect links: Sidious. ROTS Sidious > Mace (mid-high diff), and prime Sidious > Plagueis (high diff, low-medium). Plagueis ≥ ROTS Yoda (slight, low; new entry below), and Yoda > Mace (mid-high diff). Krayt vs Plagueis: low, slight Plagueis.
- What could flip it: treating Vaapad + Mace's shatterpoint sense as a real counter to Plagueis's Force game (the Mace-Sidious parity argument); a ruling that Plagueis's midi-chlorian manipulation is too slow or ritual-based to use in combat (it's disputed in t1259); a sabers-only stipulation (then Mace, mid diff).

#### Darth Malak vs the Exile (KOTOR II endgame) (2026-10-19). Base Malak: Exile, mid diff, low-medium. Star Forge Malak: toss-up, slight Exile, high diff, low
- Reasoning: The Exile's endgame wins (Sion four times, Traya on Malachor, Nihilus with Visas) are on-screen. Malak's on-screen record is losses to Revan (Leviathan aside). Karpyshyn: Malak "wasn't as strong at using the Force in other ways as Revan was". Malak's edge is raw dueling ("renowned for his combat abilities") plus the Star Forge drain of up to eight captive Jedi (K1/Viewing_Platform). The Exile's anti-drain trait is the best counter to that kind of drain.
- Common opponents: Revan. Revan > Malak (high), and Revan > Exile (now medium, see below). Traya: Exile > Traya (medium-high in-game), and SI leans Malak > Traya.
- What could flip it: taking the Hasbro "powers far greater than even Exar Kun or Freedon Nadd" question at face value (then SF Malak wins mid diff); counting the Malachor nexus fatigue against her.

#### Darth Malak vs Darth Vader (suit prime) (2026-10-19). Winner: Vader. Diff: mid vs base Malak, high vs SF Malak. Confidence: medium (base), low (SF)
- Reasoning: Vader is a better duelist with a much deeper record. Base Malak has a thin feat set. The Star Forge drain and amp (SI DarthAnt66/PeraltaEagle45 argue it is permanent; unproven) close the gap. SI t1377 is split; t2052 (base Malak vs ROTJ Vader) is mostly Vader.
- Common opponents: Exar Kun (Kun > Vader 6/10). The Malak > Kun line is the only thing linking Malak upward, and I count it as weak.
- What could flip it: the Hasbro line at full value, or a permanent Star Forge amp.

#### Darth Malak vs Dooku (ROTS) (2026-10-19). Base Malak: Dooku, mid-high diff, low-medium. SF Malak: SF Malak, high diff, low
- Reasoning: Dooku's Makashi and his record (beat Kenobi and Anakin in AOTC; held off Yoda long enough to escape) beat a base Malak who is a brute-force fighter (HK-47: Malak is "more like an angry club"). Star Forge Malak's drain-sustain outlasts him.
- Common opponents: Vader > Dooku (6.5/10), and Vader > Malak (above).
- What could flip it: counting Malak's Jedi Civil War body count as dueling skill.

#### Darth Malak (base) vs Darth Maul (TPM) (2026-10-19). Winner: Malak. Diff: mid. Confidence: low-medium (about 6.5/10)
- Reasoning: Maul is better with a blade in acrobatics but has no lightning or real drain (Smurvette75's point in t1528 is correct). Malak has the Force, lightning and durability, and he held off Revan for a while in the Star Forge duel. Maul is under Dooku (6.5/10), and base Malak is around Dooku.
- What could flip it: a sabers-only stipulation (Maul).
- Tier result: SF Malak goes to the bottom of tier 5 (around the Exile, below Kun). Base Malak goes to the top of tier 6 (just under Dooku, above Maul).

#### Darth Traya (Malachor V) vs Star Forge Malak (2026-10-19). Winner: Traya, slight. Diff: high. Confidence: low (about 5.5/10)
- Reasoning: Traya taught Revan, and both Malak and the Exile frame Revan as above Malak. Her Malachor showing includes three floating lightsabers and the Force-stripping of the Masters and Sion/Nihilus manipulation. SI t540/t2590 majority goes the other way (Malak) on the Star Forge amp and the Kun line. This one stays open.

#### Revan vs the Exile (2026-10-19, REVISED from low to medium; version split and backstab correction added later 2026-10-19 after the Revan novel). Game versions: Revan, mid-high diff, medium. Novel versions: Revan Reborn over the novel's Meetra, low-mid diff, medium-high
- Versions (peak by default; no amps on either side): (a) Game: KOTOR 1 end Revan (Jedi, light-side route) or later, vs the KOTOR II endgame Exile. (b) Novel: Revan Reborn (Revan, Ch24–28, 3,951 BBY) vs the novel's Meetra (3,951 BBY, post-KOTOR II). The novel's Meetra is a separate, lower showing: she shows none of her KOTOR II Force-bond powers. It does not move the Exile, whose tier placement stays on her KOTOR II endgame feats.
- What changed: Avellone (via the CV RT): "unless the Exile pulled some strange Force deafening move, but even that wouldn't keep Revan down for long" (author intent). In the Revan novel (Karpyshyn), Revan tells her «you have become far greater than I could ever have imagined» (Revan, Ch25, L5535). That line is about her growth since he knew her in the Mandalorian Wars, not parity. The story frames Revan as the main threat to Vitiate. Scourge kills her with a backstab while she faces the Emperor (Revan, Ch28, L6069-6071); that is not combat evidence. The SI majority puts her below Revan (t2584 unread; KingofBlades in t1100: "Meetra was fodder compared to Revan Reborn").
- Novel versions (new, 2026-10-19): Revan ashes Nyriss in one exchange (Ch24, L5425), Nyriss had Meetra «clearly overmatched» (L5399), and Meetra's own POV says «Revan's command of the Force was greater than that of anyone else she had ever met» (Ch22, L4811). Revan Reborn over the novel's Meetra: low-mid diff, medium-high confidence.
- What could flip it: her Force-bond severing used offensively; game-only Revan (KOTOR 1 end) vs KOTOR II endgame Exile (closer, toss-up). The Revan-novel worker leans mid rather than mid-high for the game versions; I kept mid-high because the novel adds nothing about the game versions.

#### Meetra Surik (the Exile) vs Darth Vader (suit prime) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Vader. Diff: high. Confidence: low-medium (about 6/10)
- Reasoning: Her best wins come with caveats. Nihilus is a hard counter for her; Traya engineered the fight and wanted to lose; Sion's win comes from talking him down. Vader's dueling and his long record against Jedi Masters run deeper. SI t1100 is a clear Vader majority (KingofBlades: "might actually favor Vader here but it would be a good fight"). Her Sion (9/10) and Vader-over-Sion (8.5/10) margins are close, so this isn't a stomp.
- What could flip it: Traya's "You are greater than any I have ever trained" + Kreia's "stronger than I" taken at full value; the Exile's Force-wound bond used to disrupt Vader's connection.

#### Meetra Surik vs Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Mace. Diff: mid-high. Confidence: low-medium
- Reasoning: Mace's Vaapad parity with ROTS Sidious tops anything the Exile has. SI t3533 majority goes Mace. S_W_LeGenD: "Mace Windu, but Meetra Surik will make him work for it".
- Tier result: the Exile stays at the bottom of tier 5, now explicitly below Revan, Vader and Mace, near SF Malak, and above Traya and Sion.

#### Luke Skywalker vs the top tiers (LotF primary-read; FotJ from the respect thread only) (2026-10-19)
- LotF Luke vs Darth Sidious (DE peak): Sidious, high diff, low-medium. FotJ Luke: toss-up. The SI majority (debates-luke.md) has FotJ Luke over DE Sidious, but FotJ is not primary-read yet.
- LotF Luke vs Plagueis: Plagueis, high diff, low. FotJ Luke vs Plagueis: Luke, mid-high diff, low. RT statements: Tila Mong "most powerful... living Jedi"; Jaina "still the most powerful Jedi in the galaxy"; Gavar Khai "one of the most powerful Jedi who had ever lived"; fold space; the beyond-shadows fights with Abeloth.
- Luke (FotJ) vs Krayt (reborn): toss-up, high diff, low. In FotJ: Apocalypse, Krayt drains both Luke and Abeloth (see the Krayt vs Plagueis entry). Krayt's reborn amp «power multiplied» offsets FotJ Luke's statements.
- Luke (FotJ) vs Abeloth: Abeloth one-on-one, high diff, low. In-story, Luke beats her with help and on prepared ground (beyond shadows).
- Luke (LotF) vs Revan (SoR/Reborn): Luke, mid diff, medium. ROTJ Luke vs Revan: Revan (SI majority).
- Luke vs Vitiate: Vitiate, mid-high diff, low. SI posters think FotJ Luke beats Valkorion; that is noted as opinion.
- Tier result: LotF Luke stays at the top of tier 5. FotJ Luke is provisionally tier 4 (low confidence) until FotJ is read.

#### Darth Maul (TPM) vs Obi-Wan Kenobi (ROTS) (2026-10-19; Darth Plagueis cite added later 2026-10-19). Winner: Obi-Wan. Diff: mid. Confidence: medium
- Versions: Maul at TPM (Legends); Obi-Wan at ROTS (Master, his peak). No amps.
- Reasoning: Padawan Obi-Wan already killed Maul in TPM. ROTS Kenobi is a Soresu master who beat Grievous and Anakin. SI t465 is a Kenobi majority (MasterCilghal: "Kenobi, high difficulty"), but that thread uses Canon SoD Maul. A TPM vs TPM rematch with no Qui-Gon trauma: Maul, mid diff, low-medium. Darth Plagueis (added 2026-10-19): Sidious's view is that Maul «had managed to kill a master sword fighter only to be overcome by a lesser one» (Darth Plagueis, Epilogue, L7317). That is about TPM (Padawan) Obi-Wan only. It supports the Maul lean in the TPM rematch and says nothing about ROTS Obi-Wan.
- What could flip it: using Canon TCW/SoD Maul growth (that's Canon, so not for the Legends tiers).

#### Darth Maul (TPM) vs Darth Vader (suit prime) (2026-10-19). Winner: Vader. Diff: mid-high. Confidence: medium (about 7/10)
- Reasoning: Maul's only edge is saber agility and speed, and the suit does limit Vader's mobility (Nova, citing Lightsabers: A Guide to the Weapons). Vader is stronger in the Force and physically, and his record goes much deeper. The SI t158 majority calls it a good fight that Vader wins. Consistent with Dooku > Maul (6.5/10) and Vader > Dooku (6.5/10).
- What could flip it: a sabers-only stipulation in cramped terrain (closer); Shadow Conspiracy's "Maul grew more powerful" claim, which is not quoted, so unverified.

#### Tier impact (2026-10-19 study)
- Malak placed for the first time: SF Malak at the bottom of tier 5, base Malak at the top of tier 6.
- The Exile stays at the bottom of tier 5. She is now explicitly below Revan, Vader and Mace; before, her placement relative to Vader and Mace was undefined.
- FotJ Luke provisionally in tier 4 (low). LotF Luke unchanged.
- Maul unchanged at the bottom of tier 6, below base Malak.
- Revised: Revan vs Exile, low -> medium (Revan).

### Four-book pass: Darth Plagueis, Revenge of the Sith (Stover novel), Labyrinth of Evil, Revan (2026-10-19)
Sources: full primary reads, in darth-plagueis-notes.md, rots-novel-notes.md, labyrinth-of-evil-notes.md and revan-novel-notes.md. Every «…» quote below is copied from those notes, where it was script-checked against the book text. Citations give book, chapter and line (L = line in that book's source file). Scale: diff is low, low-mid, mid, mid-high or high; confidence is low, low-medium, medium, medium-high or high. Peak versions by default, and each entry says whether amps are included.

#### Yoda (ROTS) vs Darth Plagueis (prime) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Plagueis, slight (near toss-up). Diff: high. Confidence: low
- Versions: Yoda at ROTS (19 BBY), his peak. Plagueis prime (Darth Plagueis Part Three, 33–32 BBY), including the permanent ~41 BBY shift amp (Darth Plagueis, Ch24, L5445: «The evidence was in his own increased midi-chlorian count»).
- For Plagueis: Sidious's POV at 54 BBY: he and Plagueis «were more than equal to the most powerful of the Jedi Order, he understood that they were no match for their combined strength» (Darth Plagueis, Ch18, L4339). That statement is about the 54 BBY versions, before the shift amp, so for prime Plagueis it is a floor. At conversation range he hid from Dooku, Sifo-Dyas, Qui-Gon and Jocasta Nu: he «drew the cloak of the profane over himself» (Ch17, L4205; 54 BBY version).
- For Yoda: Darth Plagueis has no Yoda-specific data, so the lean rests on statements. Yoda's on-page record (a high-diff loss to ROTS Sidious, see above) keeps this close.
- Common link: Sidious. ROTS Sidious > Yoda (high diff, medium) and peak Sidious > Plagueis (high diff, low-medium). The chain doesn't separate them.
- What could flip it: weighting Yoda's on-page near-standstill with Sidious over Plagueis's statement-heavy case (then Yoda, slight).

#### Darth Plagueis (67 BBY) vs Darth Venamis (67 BBY) (2026-10-19, NEW, mini-entry). Winner: Plagueis. Diff: mid. Confidence: low (the notes tag these mini-entries low; the winner is on page, the diff is the uncertain part)
- Versions: both at 67 BBY, before the shift amp; no amps.
- Evidence (Darth Plagueis, Ch6): «Tenebrous had made Venamis an expert in Plagueis's style» (L1547). Venamis «penetrated his defenses, searing the side of Plagueis's neck» (L1549). Plagueis «took himself out of his body and began working his material self like a marionette» (L1553), disarmed him, and Venamis yielded (L1549–1561).
- Side note, no verdict: Tenebrous was faster than 67 BBY Plagueis in a flat-out run («Plagueis had to call deeply on the Force merely to keep up», Ch1, L293). There's no comparative power data.

#### General Grievous (LoE, 19 BBY, before the chest crush) vs Jedi Knights (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Grievous. Diff: low. Confidence: high
- Versions: Grievous as shown in Labyrinth of Evil (19 BBY), before Mace's Force-crush of his chest at the very end of the Battle of Coruscant. This is peak Grievous, and the default. Don't merge in the 2003 *Clone Wars* Coruscant-raid kill list, which conflicts with LoE. The Knights are unnamed 19 BBY Knights. No amps (his combat computers are part of him).
- Evidence: LoE, Ch50, four Knights at once: «Compared to Mace Windu, the four were mere novices» (L4939); one beheaded, one stabbed, one dismembered, one stabbed through the heart (L4945–4955). Ch54: two Knights killed in one move, «These Jedi were more proficient than the ones he had fought in the bunker, but not skilled enough to challenge him.» (L5181–5183). Durability: «The burns did little more than add a new odor to the room.» (Ch50, L4951).
- Weak spot: the assessment is Grievous's POV, but the results back it.

#### Mace Windu (19 BBY, Vaapad) vs General Grievous (LoE, before the chest crush) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Mace. Diff: low-mid. Confidence: high
- Versions: Mace at 19 BBY with Vaapad (amp included; it's his own style). Grievous: the LoE version, before the crush.
- Evidence (LoE, Ch47, L4811–4821): Mace «was already on and all over the cyborg» (L4811). Mace's POV: Grievous's «strikes were as forceful as any Mace had ever had to counter, and his speed was astonishing. But he didn't know Vaapad» (L4813). Grievous's concession: «Tyranus had warned him about Mace Windu's prowess with a blade, and now he understood.» (Ch50, L4929).
- Why not low: Grievous's computers adapt («The result wasn't Vaapad, but it was close enough», L4817), and the fight ends on terrain plus a Force push (L4821), not on a wound.
- Counter-source: Wookieepedia's "duel Mace Windu evenly" (wiki text, grievous-legends-quotes.txt L103) is not what the novel shows.

#### Dooku (19 BBY) vs General Grievous (LoE, before the chest crush) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Dooku. Diff: mid. Confidence: medium-high
- Versions: Dooku at 19 BBY; the LoE Grievous. No amps.
- Evidence: Dooku's POV: «few, if any, Jedi would be capable of defeating him. There had been moments during the extensive combat sessions when even Dooku had been hard-pressed to outduel the cyborg.» / «But then, Dooku had kept some secrets to himself. Just in case.» (LoE, Ch22, L1669–1671). The spar demo: «He flicked his blade quickly, ridding two of the guards of their staffs, then placing the glowing tip a millimeter from Grievous's death-helmeted visage.» (Ch32, L3349). Dooku's verdict after watching him spar: «Hopeless» (L3361). Also «I pity you should you have to face off against any of the Council Masters» (L3343).

#### General Grievous (LoE, before the chest crush) vs Council Masters (Kit Fisto / Shaak Ti tier) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: the Master. Diff: mid (Shaak Ti and Stass Allie closer to high). Confidence: medium
- Versions: the LoE Grievous; Council Masters at 19 BBY. No amps.
- Evidence (LoE): Dooku's «I pity you should you have to face off against any of the Council Masters» (Ch32, L3343) and his ladder «Cin Drallig or Obi-Wan Kenobi? From Mace Windu or, stars help you, Yoda?» (L3347). Kit dismantles two MagnaGuards, «claiming a limb from both with each rotation» (Ch47, L4813–4815). Grievous ranks Kit with Mace (Ch50, L4943).
- Note: Obi-Wan specifically does better than this group; see the ROTS entry below.

#### Dooku (ROTS, 19 BBY) vs Anakin Skywalker (ROTS, pre-fall Jedi Knight), 1v1 (2026-10-19, NEW; reconciles LoE with the ROTS novel). Winner: Anakin, with his rage available. Diff: mid. Confidence: medium. Sabers only, no rage: near even, high diff, low confidence
- Versions: Dooku at 83, on the Invisible Hand. Anakin is the pre-fall Knight. His rage, the "gift of fury" he used in the ROTS novel's Ch3–4, is an amp and a separate version. The main call includes it, because pre-fall Anakin used it in this very duel. The sabers-only line excludes it.
- Evidence (ROTS novel): Dooku admits that Anakin, even now, «was holding himself back» (Ch3, L1559). Restrained Anakin is Dooku-level: «Dooku met the boy's charge easily» once taunted (Ch3, L1567). Rage-amped Anakin crushes an already exhausted Dooku: «Dooku's decades of combat experience are irrelevant. His mastery of swordplay is useless.» (Ch4, L1601; L1601–1631). Dooku's age and stamina are explicit liabilities: he «felt every hour of his eighty-three years» (Ch2, L1069; also Ch3, L1513–1517). The Council reads the result as legit: Ki-Adi-Mundi says «young Skywalker has the power to battle a Sith Lord alone, if need be; he has proven that with Dooku.» (Ch11, L3837). Mace: «Skywalker is arguably the most powerful Jedi alive, and he is still getting stronger.» (Ch8, L2941).
- Against a clean reading: the duel was rigged as a test. Sidious says «Dooku was not lost, he was sacrificed» (ROTS novel, Ch10, L3509), and in LoE he tells Dooku «Should he by some fluke best you, however, I will control the outcome to spare you any unnecessary embarrassment» (LoE, Ch55, L5261). Dooku had also fought 2v1 first. A fresh Dooku vs a fresh, raging Anakin never happens on page, so this is a lean, not a lock.
- Conflict resolved: LoE's provisional, statement-based leans were Dooku over calm Anakin (high diff) and rage-amped Anakin over Dooku (mid-high diff). The ROTS duel is direct on-page evidence, so it wins. Calm, sabers-only Anakin is now near even rather than a Dooku win, and the rage call is mid rather than mid-high. LoE still adds Dooku's view that Anakin had proved «a powerful opponent» and had «grown only more powerful since Geonosis» (LoE, Ch26, L2521).

#### Obi-Wan Kenobi (ROTS) vs General Grievous (ROTS, Utapau) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Obi-Wan. Diff: low-mid with sabers; mid-high once Obi-Wan is unarmed. Confidence: medium-high
- Versions: Obi-Wan at ROTS (19 BBY, Soresu master), his peak. Grievous on Utapau: by the LoE notes' timeline this is after the chest crush, so a lower version than LoE Grievous. The ROTS notes don't discuss the crush. No amps.
- Evidence (ROTS novel, Ch15): against twelve strikes a second, «Not one touched him.» (L6033). At twenty a second Obi-Wan counter-cuts (L6037), and one parry wrecks all the remaining sabers (L6049). Mace beforehand: «of all living Jedi, you have the best chance to defeat him» (L6015). Once Obi-Wan has lost his saber, Grievous's strength and durability make it close (L6151–6181). Ch13: Yoda: «Dangerous, Grievous is. To face him, steady minds are needed-Masters, we should send.» (L4761). Obi-Wan: «I have a feel for how he fights now-and for how he runs away.» (L4773).
- Against the LoE (pre-crush) Grievous, keep the LoE lean, Obi-Wan at mid diff (statement-based: Dooku's ladder, LoE, Ch32, L3347). The two calls are about different Grievous versions, so they don't conflict.

#### Obi-Wan Kenobi (ROTS) vs Darth Vader (unsuited Mustafar Vader) (2026-10-19, NEW). As fought: Obi-Wan, high diff, high confidence (on page). Neutral ground (no high ground, no lava): Obi-Wan, high diff, low confidence
- Versions: Obi-Wan at ROTS; Vader is the newly turned, unsuited Mustafar Vader (the peak Vader version). No amps.
- Evidence (ROTS novel, Ch20): parity: «Blade-to-blade, they were identical.» (L8413). Vader is ahead on raw power: he sends Obi-Wan's redirected bolts back «Easily, contemptuously» (L8419), plus the TK and grip (L8425, L8443–8447). Obi-Wan's edges carry over to neutral ground: the polarity trick disarms Vader (L8431–8435), «The flaw of power is arrogance.» (L8435), and the feint-and-dive bait that leaves Vader «Half a second too slow» (L8569–8573). The loss is framed as arrogance, a trait of the character, not of the terrain.
- Weak spot: Obi-Wan's «you have far surpassed my humble efforts at instruction» (Ch13, L4931) is a modest teacher's line, not a power ranking. This is the closest call in the four books.

#### Revan vs Vitiate, Revan-novel versions (2026-10-19, NEW). Revan Reborn vs the base Emperor: Vitiate, mid diff, high confidence. Revan Reborn vs the Emperor feeding on Revan: Vitiate, low-mid diff, low confidence. DK1 Revan (+ Malak): Vitiate, low diff, high confidence. Revan + Meetra + Scourge (+ T3) vs the base Emperor: unresolved, lean Vitiate, high diff, low confidence
- Versions: Revan Reborn = memories restored by the mask, balanced «on the knife-edge between them, drawing on both the light and dark sides for strength» (Revan, Ch27, L5803), 3,951 BBY. He is the novel's peak Revan, with no amp. The base Emperor is post-Nathema Vitiate as of 3,951 BBY, before he feeds on Revan. The Nathema ritual is included, since every later version has it. The fed Emperor feeds on Revan from Ch29 on («Revan could feel the Emperor feeding on him, drawing on his power to sate his endless hunger», Ch29, L6189). That is a separate, amped version, and the size of the boost is unquantified. DK1 Revan is Revan, with Malak, on the first Dromund Kaas visit (~3,959 BBY, after the Mandalorian Wars, before the Jedi Civil War). He is not the Jedi Civil War Darth Revan used in Sith lists.
- Reborn vs base (on page, Ch28): Revan knocks the Emperor back once while his strength is diverted («The Emperor, unprepared and with much of his strength diverted to his effort to dominate Revan's mind, was sent flying backward», L5987). He hits him with a redirected bolt that leaves «his robes smoking and singed» (L5995–5997). Then he loses the lightning clash, because «the Emperor was infinitely more powerful than Darth Nyriss had ever been» (L6001). He is left «Helpless» (L6019), and only T3 and Meetra save him. It's mid, not high, because the Emperor took no real damage.
- DK1: «he didn't even have to fight us. Instead, he broke our wills» (Ch25, L5601); «In their last meeting he had overwhelmed Revan completely; it wasn't even fair to call it a battle» (Ch27, L5859). Version link, from Revan, who knew both: «Revan had grown since then. He was far more powerful now» (L5859).
- 3v1: never fought. Scourge thinks «the Emperor would have won regardless» (Ch29, L6129). Revan thinks «They might have lost anyway, but they also might have defeated the Emperor» (L6201). The fight ended on Scourge's backstab (Ch28, L6069-6071).
- What could flip it: the fed Emperor's boost could be larger than assumed; the 3v1 is deliberately left open by the author.

#### Revan Reborn vs Lord Scourge (mortal) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Revan. Diff: low. Confidence: high
- Versions: Revan Reborn (3,951 BBY). Scourge is mortal, before the Ch29 immortality ritual. No amps. Scourge's emotion-feeding talent is innate («The greater your opponent's connection to the Force, the stronger you become», Revan, Ch8, L1741, said by Nyriss).
- Evidence: Revan ashes Nyriss in one exchange (Ch24, L5425), and Nyriss had «Scourge barely managed to parry the first wave of her assault» (L5397). Scourge's POV: «If anyone had the strength to stop the Emperor, it was this man.» (L5437). To the Emperor: «I knew I was not strong enough to defeat him myself» (Ch28, L6079). That was part of a lie, but it matches L5437.
- Exception: the drugged, unarmed captive Revan («unarmed he was no match for the Sith», Ch24, L5307).

#### The Revan novel's Meetra Surik vs Lord Scourge (mortal) (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: toss-up, slight Meetra. Diff: high. Confidence: low
- Versions: the novel's Meetra (3,951 BBY, post-KOTOR II Jedi Master), a separate, lower showing than the KOTOR II endgame Exile; Scourge mortal. No amps.
- For Meetra: Scourge was «impressed with how easily she had dismantled Murtog and his handpicked team» (Revan, Ch21, L4553). She disarmed the Emperor by surprise, «knocking it from the Emperor's grasp» (Ch28, L6035), while a less-than-a-second mind-brush floored Scourge (Ch23, L5075).
- For Scourge: the emotion-feeding talent (Ch8, L1741); «Scourge was an expert swordsman» (Ch27, L5939).
- Even: both did about the same against Nyriss (Ch24, L5397–5399) and the Imperial Guard. Scourge's POV: «He didn't know which of them would prove the stronger» (Ch21, L4557). The backstab (L6069) isn't evidence. The KOTOR II endgame Exile vs Scourge isn't judged here.

#### Revan Reborn vs Darth Nyriss (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Revan. Diff: low. Confidence: high
- Versions: Revan Reborn, minutes after the mask restored his memories (Ch24); Nyriss «in the prime of her powers» (Revan, Ch12, L2607). No amps.
- Evidence (Revan, Ch24): «A dozen bolts of lightning sprang from Nyriss's hand... Instead of leaping back into the cell to avoid the deadly attack, Revan stepped forward to intercept it» (L5419); «the bolts ripped it apart and continued on unabated... leaving only a pile of charred ash» (L5425). She was dead in one exchange.

#### Darth Nyriss vs Lord Scourge + the novel's Meetra, 2v1 (2026-10-19, NEW). Winner: Nyriss. Diff: mid. Confidence: medium
- Versions: Nyriss prime; Scourge mortal; the novel's Meetra. No amps.
- Evidence (Revan, Ch24, L5393–5415): «Scourge barely managed to parry the first wave of her assault» (L5397); «The Jedi was clearly overmatched; though she managed to hold her ground, she was forced down to one knee» (L5399); in Scourge's POV, «Nyriss was too powerful; her command of the dark side was too strong» (L5411). Both got barriers up (L5403, L5407), so they weren't helpless, just outclassed. Revan interrupted before the finish.
- Confidence is my call: it's a single on-page fight, and the notes found no real caveats.

#### Tier impact (2026-10-19, four-book pass)
- No tier moves for existing placements. Plagueis stays in tier 4 and is now at its top (the #3 Sith); Yoda vs Plagueis is judged, and Yoda vs Krayt is still open.
- Vader is now split into versions (see the tier list): unsuited Mustafar Vader is above suited Vader.
- Grievous is placed provisionally (LoE version): bottom of tier 6 or top of tier 7.
- Nyriss is added to "Not placed yet", around low tier 5 / high tier 6. The novel's Meetra is a separate, lower showing, so the Exile stays at the bottom of tier 5.

## Star Wars (Legends) tier rankings (draft, revised 2026-10-12 to place Yoda and Mace; version notes, Grievous and Nyriss added 2026-10-19). Confidence: low-medium
1. The Father / the Son (Mortis Ones, Force embodiments; if counted)
2. Vitiate/Valkorion (version note 2026-10-19: base Emperor at 3,951 BBY < the Emperor feeding on Revan, from Revan Ch29 L6189 on < SWTOR/Valkorion; the tier-2 slot uses the SWTOR/Valkorion peak, with amps included)
3. Sidious (Dark Empire peak) ~ Abeloth. ROTS Sidious sits on the 3/4 line.
4. Plagueis (prime) ≥ Yoda (ROTS prime) ~ Krayt (reborn). Yoda is just under ROTS Sidious (Sidious, high diff, medium; see above). Yoda vs Plagueis is now judged (Plagueis, slight; high diff, low confidence; 2026-10-19), so Plagueis sits at the top of tier 4 as the #3 Sith. Yoda vs Krayt is still NOT judged. Plagueis version note: "Plagueis prime" is Part Three of Darth Plagueis (33–32 BBY), after the ~41 BBY shift amp (Darth Plagueis, Ch24, L5445). The 67 BBY version is far weaker: he could perceive midi-chlorians «though not yet the ability to manipulate them» (Ch1, L377).
5. Luke (LotF era), then Darth Caedus (Invincible era) just below him; Starkiller/Galen Marek (TFU peak) is placed in tier 5 above Vader (medium) and below Luke (low) (Luke > Caedus, high confidence; see the entries above); Vader; Revan; Nihilus; Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad). Mace's ceiling is a saber stalemate with ROTS Sidious, but Yoda is above him (Yoda, mid-high diff). His place inside tier 5 is open: Mace vs Vader and Mace vs Revan aren't done. Nihilus: wound-in-the-Force planet drain (Katarr) but lost to the Exile + Visas, a hard counter (KOTOR Campaign Guide; Complete SW Encyclopedia). Exar Kun (living, Sith War) added 2026-10-18 to tier 5, lower half: below Revan Reborn (Revan, high diff, low-medium) and Luke/Caedus, above ROTJ suited Vader (Kun, high diff, medium) and Dooku (Kun, mid diff, medium). Spirit Kun (Jedi Academy era) sits around tier 6. Added 2026-10-19: Star Forge Malak and the Exile (Meetra) sit at the bottom of tier 5 (Exile below Revan medium, Vader low-medium and Mace; SF Malak below Kun, ~Exile). FotJ Luke is provisionally tier 4 (low; not primary-read yet). The Exile's slot is based on her KOTOR II endgame feats. The Revan novel's Meetra is a separate, lower showing and does not move her (2026-10-19).
   - Vader version note (2026-10-19): "Vader" in tier 5 means the suited prime (ROTJ/comics). The unsuited Mustafar Vader is the stronger version in Force power. The ROTS novel tells the newly suited Vader «you are so far less now than what you were» (ROTS novel, Ch21, L8867). But Obi-Wan beat the unsuited Vader (on page, and narrowly on neutral ground), so his exact slot is not set. The newly suited Vader of late ROTS is about Dooku's level (tier 6).
   - Revan version note (2026-10-19): KOTOR 1 Revan is a Jedi unless on the dark-side route. Sith lists use Darth Revan from the Jedi Civil War. Ladder: DK1 Revan (dominated by Vitiate, ~3,959 BBY) and Darth Revan (Jedi Civil War peak) < KOTOR 1 end Revan (Malak: «stronger than you ever were during your reign as the Dark Lord», K1/Viewing_Platform). Revan Reborn (3,951 BBY) is the novel's peak. Revan himself says he was «far more powerful now» than at DK1 (Revan, Ch27, L5859), but nobody who knew both versions compares Reborn with KOTOR 1 end Revan. Tier-5 Revan = Revan Reborn.
6. Dooku (ROTS era): just under Mace (Mace, high diff) and unsuited Mustafar Vader (Vader, mid diff), about even with the newly suited Vader, and above TPM Maul (Dooku, mid diff). Pre-fall Anakin (rage available) beats him at mid diff (2026-10-19). Clear losses to Yoda and Sidious. Moved to DEEP 2026-10-17. Base Malak (no Star Forge) sits at the top of tier 6, just under Dooku (Dooku mid-high diff) and above Maul (Malak mid diff), added 2026-10-19. Darth Maul (TPM) sits at the bottom of tier 6 (below Dooku and living Kun, above Sion, low-medium), added 2026-10-18. General Grievous (LoE, 19 BBY, before the chest crush) is placed provisionally at the bottom of tier 6 or the top of tier 7, below Dooku (Dooku, mid diff) and Mace (Mace, low-mid diff), added 2026-10-19. Grievous vs Maul and Grievous vs Sion are not judged (LoE worker's reasoning-only lean: Maul, mid-high diff). ROTS (Utapau) Grievous is a lower showing.
7. Darth Sion (top of tier 7): below Maul (low-medium), Nihilus (Nihilus, mid diff), the Exile (the Exile, low diff) and Vader (Vader, low diff). Immortality on a dark-side world is a modifier, not raw power.
Not placed yet: Naga Sadow, Ulic, Ragnos and the other INTRO-only characters. Added 2026-10-19: Darth Nyriss (Revan novel, 3,951 BBY), around low tier 5 / high tier 6. She beat Scourge and the novel's Meetra together (mid diff), and Revan Reborn ashed her (low diff). That creates tension with the Exile's tier-5 slot, resolved by treating the novel's Meetra as a separate, lower showing. Lord Scourge (mortal) sits about level with the novel's Meetra. ROTS Obi-Wan is not placed: he beats unsuited Mustafar Vader (high diff), ROTS Grievous (low-mid with sabers) and TPM Maul (mid).
Reasoning: on-page outcomes plus reliable framing first, hype (with recency discounts) second. Many pairs in tiers 4-5 aren't settled.
